The same platform-linked ordering NPIs appear on claims to Medicare, TRICARE, and VA community care simultaneously. Multiple distinct L-code braces per beneficiary are delivered within a rolling 30-day window. New supplier and pharmacy NPIs reach peer-top-decile paid dollars within one quarter of enrolment.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists; action prepay edit. 2) Cross-payer orderer overlap: on ordering NPI x month, compute the distinct count of payers and distinct billing NPIs carrying its orders; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Rapid-ramp new biller: on supplier or pharmacy NPI x quarter, compute paid dollars divided by months since PECOS enrolment approval; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action site visit and prior-authorisation requirement.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Pennsylvania
FraudEntity: Thomas Stafford (Chief Executive Officer and President of Information Systems Staffing, Inc.); Information Systems Staffing, Inc.
SchemeSummary: Stafford, CEO of an IT staffing company, allegedly caused the company to fail to pay over approximately $2,008,046.63 in trust fund taxes (Social Security, Medicare and federal income tax withholdings from employee paychecks) to the IRS from Q1 2019 through Q4 2024, while using company bank accounts to pay personal expenses; he also allegedly understated income and concealed control of properties in a 2023 Chapter 13 bankruptcy filing.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim here and no payer adjudication point, since the loss is unremitted payroll trust fund taxes. The nearest detection route is IRS matching of W-2 withholding totals filed with SSA against Form 941 filings and EFTPS deposits per EIN. A second route is bankruptcy trustee comparison of schedules against county property deed records and business bank account statements.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) W-2 to 941 reconciliation: on employer EIN x quarter, compute the difference between withholding reported on W-2/W-3 filings and tax deposited via EFTPS plus Form 941 liability; fires when the gap is nonzero for consecutive quarters; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
FraudEntity: Dr. Kingsley R. Chin (Founder, President and CEO of SpineFrontier, Inc.); SpineFrontier, Inc. (medical device company)
FraudTypeAll: kickback_Bribery For Referral; Falsify certificate; Device, DME
SchemeSummary: SpineFrontier offered spine surgeons purported product-development consulting arrangements; Chin directed employees to report to CMS's Open Payments Program a $4,750 payment made to a surgeon on Jan. 19, 2016 as a 'consulting' fee, though he knew no actual consulting work had been performed, concealing the true nature of the payment required to be publicly disclosed under the Physician Payment Sunshine Act.
WaysToIdentify: At Open Payments reconciliation, consulting payments to a surgeon NPI carry no deliverable, invoice, or hours record in the manufacturer's contract file. The paid surgeon NPIs are the same NPIs whose hospital implant logs show the manufacturer's spinal devices in the following quarter. Payment amounts repeat as identical round figures across many surgeon recipients on the same reporting date. Device-specific HCPCS or charge-master implant lines at the surgeons' facilities rise after the first Open Payments consulting entry. The manufacturer's CMS-855 and ownership disclosures show physician-owned entities receiving the transfers rather than the physicians directly.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Pay-to-implant correlation: on surgeon NPI x manufacturer, compute the Spearman correlation between quarterly Open Payments consulting dollars and quarterly implanted-device claim volume on that manufacturer's spinal codes; fires when correlation is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 2) Undocumented consulting: on Open Payments record, compute the count of supporting deliverables, invoices, and logged hours attached in the manufacturer's contract file; fires when that count is zero; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Surgeon-consultant volume shift: on surgeon NPI x quarter, compute spinal implant procedure counts versus the surgeon's own trailing twelve-month baseline; fires when the increase exceeds the baseline and consulting payments began that quarter; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
FraudEntity: Dr. Kingsley R. Chin (Founder, President and CEO of SpineFrontier, Inc.); SpineFrontier, Inc.; KICVentures
FraudTypeAll: kickback_Bribery For Referral; Falsify certificate; Device, DME
SchemeSummary: Chin, CEO of medical device maker SpineFrontier, offered surgeons purported product-development consulting engagements and directed employees to report a $4,750 payment to a surgeon on Jan. 19, 2016 as a 'consulting' fee in CMS Open Payments reporting under the Physician Payment Sunshine Act, though he knew no actual consulting work had been performed. He was sentenced to one year supervised release (first six months home confinement), a $9,500 fine, plus $40,000 personally and $855,000 from his company KICVentures in a related civil settlement.
WaysToIdentify: At Open Payments validation, the reported nature-of-payment category is 'consulting' but no contract deliverable or timesheet exists in the manufacturer's file. Recipient surgeon NPIs bill the manufacturer's spinal implant codes at facilities in the quarters following each payment. Identical round-dollar payments recur across multiple surgeon recipients, a pattern visible in the Open Payments general payment file. Payments flow to physician-owned intermediary entities disclosed on the manufacturer's ownership records rather than to the physician NPI. Implant utilisation at recipient surgeons exceeds their own trailing baseline after the first payment date.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Consulting-without-deliverable: on Open Payments payment record, compute the count of matched invoices, hours logged, and deliverables in the manufacturer's contract repository; fires when the count is zero; action postpay audit. 2) Referral-payment coupling: on surgeon NPI x manufacturer x quarter, compute the ratio of that manufacturer's implant claim lines to the surgeon's total implant lines before and after first payment; fires when the post-payment ratio exceeds the pre-payment ratio and is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 3) Round-amount clustering: on manufacturer TIN x payment date, compute the distinct count of recipient NPIs receiving an identical payment amount; fires when that count is above the calibrated percentile versus peer manufacturers; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Washington
SchemeSummary: Not a fraud case: this press release announces the appointment of Charles Neil Floyd as interim U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Washington and describes his career, with no fraud scheme described.
WaysToIdentify: This item describes a personnel appointment, so there is no claim, no billed service, and no adjudication point. No payer signal exists to observe in claims, enrolment, or prior-authorisation data. The nearest non-claims route is routine records classification that excludes non-case announcements from fraud intake.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Route such announcements out of the fraud referral queue at intake triage.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of North Carolina
FraudEntity: Steven Osbey (co-owner, Reign & Inspirations, LLC); Aljihad Shabazz (co-owner); Reign & Inspirations, LLC (clinic)
SchemeSummary: Co-owners of a Charlotte clinic billed NC Medicaid for in-home physician visits that never occurred, submitting more than 30,000 hours of purported visits, at times billing over 100 one-hour in-home visits by a single physician in one day. Osbey consented to a $4,711,159 civil judgment; co-owner Shabazz pleaded guilty to health care fraud conspiracy and money laundering and received 52 months in prison.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, summing timed home-visit CPT units by rendering NPI per date of service yields more than 24 hours in a day. The rendering physician NPI appears on visits at beneficiary addresses too far apart to travel between within the billed times. Place of service 12 home visits dominate the practice's claim mix versus same-specialty peers in the Medicaid claim file. No corresponding beneficiary claims exist from pharmacies, labs, or hospitals near the purported visit dates. The rendering NPI is simultaneously listed on facility claims elsewhere on the same dates of service.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Impossible-day hours: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of billed time-based units converted to minutes across all claim lines; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) Travel infeasibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the minimum driving time needed to visit all billed beneficiary residence addresses in sequence; fires when required travel plus billed service minutes exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Home-visit concentration: on provider NPI x month, compute the share of claim lines with place of service 12 and the distinct beneficiary count; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Virginia
FraudEntity: Chesapeake Regional Medical Center (hospital, formerly Chesapeake Regional Hospital); Javaid Perwaiz (physician, OB/GYN with privileges at CRMC)
PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid (Virginia Department of Medical Assistance Services); TRICARE; Anthem; Optima; Humana; Cigna; Aetna; United
SchemeSummary: CRMC allegedly kept granting and re-credentialing privileges to Dr. Javaid Perwaiz from 1984 to 2019 despite knowing he had been terminated elsewhere for unnecessary surgeries and had federal felony convictions, and collected roughly $18.5 million from Medicare, Medicaid/Virginia DMAS, TRICARE and commercial insurers for his medically unnecessary hysterectomies and other procedures, elective pre-39-week inductions/C-sections supported by obstetric flowsheets with fabricated due dates (about 64% of reviewed 2019 Medicaid forms altered), sterilizations of Medicaid patients without valid consent forms, and inpatient-only surgeries misclassified and billed as outpatient. Perwaiz was separately convicted in 2020 on 52 counts and sentenced to 59 years; the hospital is now indicted for health care fraud and conspiracy.
WaysToIdentify: At credentialing, the practitioner NPI matches an OIG LEIE entry or a prior felony disclosure on the CMS-855 adverse-legal-action fields. Hysterectomy and sterilisation rates per attending NPI far exceed same-specialty peers in the facility's inpatient and outpatient claim file. Medicaid sterilisation claims lack a valid, timely signed HHS-687 consent form in the prior-authorisation record. Deliveries billed before 39 weeks carry gestational dates on obstetric flowsheets that contradict earlier prenatal ultrasound and E/M claim dates. Procedures on the CMS inpatient-only list are billed with outpatient bill types at the same facility.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Exclusion and adverse-action match: on rendering NPI at credentialing, compute exact matches against OIG LEIE, state licence board discipline files, and NPPES/PECOS adverse-action entries; fires on any exact identity match; action claim suspension. 2) Procedure-rate outlier: on attending NPI x quarter, compute hysterectomy and sterilisation claim lines divided by that NPI's total female patient encounters; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit with documentation request (ADR). 3) Consent and gestational-age integrity: on claim line for sterilisation or pre-39-week delivery, compute the day gap between consent-form signature date and procedure date and the difference between flowsheet due date and earliest prenatal ultrasound dating; fires when the consent window is violated or the dating differs beyond clinical tolerance; action prepay edit. 4) Inpatient-only misclassification: on claim line, compute whether the billed procedure code appears on the CMS inpatient-only list while the bill type is outpatient; fires on exact list match; action prepay edit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Virginia
FraudEntity: David Neel (sole owner and operator of Siesta Health LLC, Healthy Sleep LLC, and Healthy Sleep Partners, LLC)
SchemeSummary: Neel, owner of several central Virginia sleep disorder centers, withheld at least $311,985 in federal trust fund taxes from employees' wages (issuing W-2s reflecting the withholding) but never filed Form 941s or paid the funds over to the IRS, and also failed to pay at least $148,558 of the employer's Medicare and Social Security share, using company funds instead for personal expenses such as rent on a horse farm, life insurance, tuition, and a truck.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, because the loss is withheld employee payroll taxes never remitted. The clearest non-claims signal is SSA W-2 withholding totals for the EIN with no corresponding Form 941 filed for those quarters. A second route is the absence of any EFTPS deposits for an EIN that continues to report active payroll.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) Nonfiler withholding gap: on employer EIN x quarter, compute W-2 reported withholding minus Form 941 filings and EFTPS deposits; fires when 941 filings are absent while W-2 withholding is positive; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
FraudEntity: Dr. Stanley L. Librach (physician); Dr. Asim Muhammad Ali (physician); Jerry Dale Leech (chiropractor); Denis J. Mikhlin (business owner); Central Diagnostic Laboratory (CDL)
State_County: Missouri - St. Louis County (Chesterfield, Creve Coeur); Missouri - St. Louis
SchemeSummary: Physicians Librach and Ali and chiropractor Leech referred urine samples to Central Diagnostic Laboratory in exchange for kickbacks routed to entities owned by Leech and Mikhlin (including Ali paying the wages of Librach's clinic employees), with CDL billing Medicare and Medicaid for the testing; in a second scheme the doctors pre-signed oxycodone and other controlled-substance prescriptions one day a week without examining patients or reviewing charts, knowing pharmacies would bill Medicare and Medicaid. Librach was sentenced to 5 years and ordered to repay $2.87 million; co-defendant Mikhlin was previously sentenced to 9 years and ordered to repay $181,265, and other defendants await sentencing.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, a single laboratory NPI receives nearly all urine drug testing referrals from a tiny set of ordering NPIs, visible in the referral graph. Definitive drug testing panels are billed with maximum analyte counts on every beneficiary regardless of diagnosis. A chiropractor NPI appears as ordering provider on toxicology claims outside chiropractic scope under the state licence board file. Controlled-substance prescriptions from an ordering NPI cluster on one weekday with no same-day E/M claim for those beneficiaries. Payroll or payment flows between the laboratory's owners and the ordering clinics appear on CMS-855 ownership and managing-control disclosures.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Referral concentration graph: on laboratory NPI x quarter, compute the share of toxicology claim lines from the top ordering NPIs and each orderer's share sent to that lab; fires when both concentration measures are above the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action payment suspension. 2) Order-without-encounter for controlled substances: on beneficiary x prescriber NPI x fill date, compute the day gap to the nearest E/M claim by that prescriber; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit on the Part D claim. 3) Same-weekday prescribing burst: on prescriber NPI x day of week, compute the count of controlled-substance prescriptions written divided by that prescriber's daily average; fires when a single weekday exceeds the provider's own trailing baseline by the calibrated multiple; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Wyoming
FraudEntity: Sean P. Madigan (coffee shop operator); Victoria Madigan (spouse)
FraudTypeAll: Covid or General Loan Fraud; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud; Wire Fraud
SchemeSummary: A married couple failed to disclose income from their Cheyenne Frontier Mall coffee shop when certifying eligibility for Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher assistance from the Cheyenne Housing Authority (a HUD-jurisdiction matter), and Sean Madigan used the coffee shop to fraudulently obtain State of Wyoming COVID-19 business relief grant funds, spending a material portion on household living expenses rather than business purposes. Both received five years supervised probation; restitution figures span both defendants ($161,175 to the State of Wyoming from Sean plus $12,864 joint and several to the Cheyenne Housing Authority).
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point, since the programs are HUD housing vouchers and a state COVID business grant. The nearest detection route is matching tenant-certified income on HUD Form 50058 against IRS and state wage and business-income records. A second route is comparing grant disbursement bank accounts against personal expenditure patterns before funds are released.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) Income certification mismatch: on household x recertification date, compute certified annual income on HUD-50058 minus reported wage, 1099, and Schedule C income; fires when the difference is nonzero beyond the allowed tolerance; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois
FraudEntity: Clarence W. Brown III (chiropractor, owner of Dr. CB3 Wellness, Inc. and Apex Integrated Medical Center, Ltd.); Dr. CB3 Wellness, Inc.; Apex Integrated Medical Center, Ltd.
PayerName: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Illinois
SchemeSummary: Brown submitted more than 6,000 fraudulent claims to Blue Cross Blue Shield of Illinois through his two Chicago clinics for health care services never provided, including services purportedly rendered while he was on international vacations or while his medical license was suspended, netting nearly $2.1 million used for a house, a $100,000 BMW, vacations and luxury shopping.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, dates of service fall inside licence suspension periods recorded in the state licence board file for the rendering NPI. Dates of service overlap the rendering provider's international travel, evidenced by absence of any other provider activity plus border-crossing records. Claim volume per rendering NPI per day exceeds feasible treatment minutes for timed chiropractic CPT codes. Treated beneficiaries have no corroborating claims from other providers such as imaging or pharmacy around the visit dates. Claims are submitted in large identical batches with repeating code sequences across unrelated beneficiaries.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Licence-status date check: on claim line, compute whether the date of service falls between the suspension start and reinstatement dates in the state licence board file for the rendering NPI; fires on any exact overlap; action prepay edit. 2) Daily capacity: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of timed CPT minutes across all claim lines; fires when the total exceeds a feasible clinic day; action claim suspension. 3) Template batch detection: on provider NPI x submission batch, compute the distinct count of unique code sequences divided by the number of beneficiaries; fires when the ratio falls below the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois
FraudEntity: Zishan Alvi (owner/operator of Chicago Covid-19 testing laboratory)
State_County: Illinois - Cook County (Chicago); defendant resided in Inverness, Ill.
PayerName: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services' Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA)
FraudTypeAll: Phantom Claims; Covid or General Loan Fraud; Wire Fraud
SchemeSummary: Alvi's Chicago lab submitted tens of thousands of claims to HRSA's Covid-19 program for tests that were never performed or were inconclusive because he diluted test reagents to cut costs, while releasing negative results to patients and lying to lab directors to conceal it; HRSA paid the lab over $14 million. He was sentenced to 84 months, ordered to pay over $14.1 million restitution and forfeit over $8 million in cash plus three vehicles.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, claimed COVID test volume per day exceeds the lab's instrument throughput declared on its CLIA certificate and CMS-855B enrolment. Uninsured-program claims lack matching specimen accession identifiers or reagent lot consumption in the lab's LIS records. Reagent purchase volume from wholesaler invoices is far below the number of tests billed. The lab's positivity rate is a statistical outlier versus other labs in the same county over the same weeks. Billed patient rosters include repeated demographic patterns and addresses inconsistent with genuine uninsured attestations.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Throughput impossibility: on laboratory NPI x date of service, compute billed test claim lines divided by validated instrument capacity from CLIA and 855B equipment declarations; fires when the ratio exceeds one; action prepay edit. 2) Reagent-to-test reconciliation: on laboratory NPI x month, compute tests billed minus tests supportable by reagent units purchased on wholesaler invoices; fires when the difference is positive; action payment suspension. 3) Positivity outlier: on laboratory NPI x week, compute the positive result share among billed COVID tests versus the county mean for the same week; fires when deviation is above the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs; U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois
FraudEntity: Zishan Alvi (owner and operator of Chicago laboratory)
PayerName: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services' Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) COVID-19 uninsured program
FraudTypeAll: Phantom Claims; Covid or General Loan Fraud; Wire Fraud
SchemeSummary: Alvi's Chicago lab billed HRSA for COVID-19 tests that were never performed or were diluted to save costs, releasing negative results to patients even when specimens were untested or results inconclusive, and he lied to lab directors to conceal it; HRSA paid over $14 million. Restitution of $14,199,217 plus forfeiture of approximately $6.8 million cash, a Range Rover, and over $630,000 from an E-Trade account were ordered.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, uninsured-program test claims exceed the specimen accession count recorded in the laboratory information system for the same dates. Reagent quantities purchased from wholesalers cannot support the volume of tests billed that month. Daily billed volume exceeds analyser capacity declared on the CLIA certificate and CMS-855B enrolment. Reported result distributions show almost no inconclusive results, an outlier versus peer labs in the same weeks. Uninsured attestation records lack verifiable patient identifiers or duplicate the same demographics across many claims.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Accession reconciliation: on laboratory NPI x date of service, compute billed test claim lines minus distinct specimen accession IDs in the LIS; fires when the difference is positive; action claim suspension. 2) Reagent supply ceiling: on laboratory NPI x month, compute the maximum tests supportable by purchased reagent units from wholesaler pedigree data and subtract billed tests; fires when billed exceeds supportable; action payment suspension. 3) Inconclusive-rate outlier: on laboratory NPI x week, compute the share of reported inconclusive or invalid results among billed tests; fires when below the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of California
FraudEntity: Fernando Valenzuela Ayub (owner/operator of DME companies); co-conspirators (nominee owners of DME companies); sham marketing companies
State_County: California - San Diego County (Chula Vista/San Diego)
FraudTypeAll: Device, DME; kickback_Bribery For Referral; Wire Fraud; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud; Falsify certificate
SchemeSummary: Valenzuela and co-conspirators operated multiple DME companies that billed Medicare roughly $51 million (paid ~$20 million) for orthotic braces obtained through $3.7 million in kickbacks to sham marketing companies supplying bogus prescriptions; after his companies were suspended from billing, he placed new DME companies in nominee owners' names while retaining control and laundered at least $14 million of Medicare proceeds.
WaysToIdentify: At enrolment, the CMS-855S owners, authorised officials, and bank accounts of a new supplier match those of a previously suspended supplier NPI. Brace L-code claims carry ordering NPIs with no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary. Beneficiary residence ZIPs are scattered nationwide, far outside the supplier's declared service area. A handful of ordering NPIs supply orders across many nominally unrelated supplier NPIs. Payments route to bank accounts shared across multiple supplier TINs in the EFT authorisation records.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Nominee-owner linkage: on new supplier NPI at enrolment, compute the count of shared addresses, phone numbers, bank accounts, and authorised officials with any suspended or revoked supplier in PECOS; fires when any exact match exists; action claim suspension plus site visit. 2) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the nearest E/M claim between that ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 3) Shared-bank-account graph: on bank account, compute the distinct count of supplier NPIs and TINs receiving EFT payments; fires when the count exceeds one without disclosed common ownership; action payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Tennessee
FraudEntity: Thomas K. Weir (majority owner, Oakley Pharmacy d/b/a Dale Hollow Pharmacy and Clay County Xpress Pharmacy); William L. Donaldson (former owner and pharmacist of Dale Hollow Pharmacy, then Donaldson Pharmacy); Pamela Spivey (co-owner of Clay County Xpress Pharmacy); Charles Robert 'Bobby' Oakley (minority owner, Dale Hollow Pharmacy); John Polston (pharmacist-in-charge); Michael Griffith (pharmacist-in-charge)
SchemeSummary: Owners and pharmacists-in-charge of two Celina, Tennessee pharmacies dispensed high volumes of controlled substances despite obvious signs of abuse and diversion, and billed Medicare Part D and TennCare for medically unnecessary combinations of controlled substances; they also paid patient co-payments, paid cash and gave 'Monkey Bucks' redeemable for cash to induce patients to fill prescriptions there, and Donaldson received kickbacks for recruiting patients. Weir agreed to pay $1,419,974 restitution and forfeit pharmacy-related properties; six defendants pleaded guilty in total, none yet sentenced.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, the pharmacy NDC mix shows opioid, benzodiazepine, and muscle relaxant trinity combinations far above peer pharmacies. Cash-equivalent inducements appear as zero copay collected on Part D claims despite required cost sharing in the remittance record. Beneficiaries travel unusual distances to this pharmacy, measured from residence ZIP to pharmacy ZIP on the claim. ARCOS and wholesaler pedigree data show controlled-substance purchase volumes above the calibrated percentile for the pharmacy's dispensing population. Multiple prescribers write nearly identical controlled-substance regimens filled almost exclusively at this pharmacy.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Trinity combination rate: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of beneficiaries with overlapping opioid, benzodiazepine, and carisoprodol days supply across NDCs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer pharmacies; action prepay edit. 2) Copay waiver detection: on beneficiary x pharmacy NPI, compute the share of Part D claims with patient-paid amount of zero where cost sharing was owed; fires when the share exceeds the pharmacy's own trailing baseline and peer norm; action postpay audit. 3) Patient draw distance: on pharmacy NPI x quarter, compute the median miles from beneficiary residence ZIP to the pharmacy for controlled-substance fills; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer pharmacies; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas
FraudEntity: Dempsey Spears (owner of Transitional Life Counseling and Consultation and Spears Community Services)
State_County: Texas - Galveston County (Texas City); Texas - Dallas County (Mesquite); Texas - Harris County (Houston)
SchemeSummary: Owner of two mental health clinics allegedly billed Medicare roughly $4 million (paid about $1.5 million) for psychotherapy services never provided, continuing to bill under the identities of seven licensed clinical social workers after they resigned, and submitting claims for beneficiaries who were already deceased on the dates of the billed treatment.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, the date of service is later than the beneficiary's date of death in the Death Master File and Medicare enrolment record. The rendering NPI's state licence board file shows no active affiliation, and NPPES shows a changed practice address after resignation. Psychotherapy CPT units per rendering NPI per day exceed feasible therapy minutes in a 24-hour period. The clinic bills the same rendering NPIs continuously with no gaps, unlike normal clinician schedules with absences. Rendering clinicians simultaneously appear on claims from unrelated employers in other cities on identical dates.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Deceased beneficiary edit: on claim line, compute the day gap between date of service and the date of death in the Death Master File and enrolment database; fires when the service date is after death; action prepay edit. 2) Rendering-clinician capacity: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total psychotherapy CPT minutes summed across all payers; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours or the licensed workday; action claim suspension. 3) Departed-clinician billing: on rendering NPI x billing TIN, compute the count of claim lines dated after the clinician's last verified employment or licence affiliation date; fires when that count is above zero; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Washington
FraudEntity: Dr. David Antonio Becerril (licensed Washington physician who signed prescriptions); Real Time Physicians, LLC (telemarketing company); Marc Sporn (former owner of Real Time Physicians, LLC)
State_County: Washington - Yakima County (Selah); Idaho - Kootenai County (Coeur d'Alene); Florida - Palm Beach County (Delray Beach)
FraudTypeAll: Falsify certificate; Phantom Claims; Device, DME; kickback_Bribery For Referral; IdentityFraud
SchemeSummary: Real Time Physicians telemarketers cold-called elderly Medicare beneficiaries to harvest their personal and Medicare beneficiary numbers, then had Dr. Becerril certify pre-prepared prescriptions through an internet portal (reviewed on average 26 seconds each) for genetic tests and back, knee, shoulder and ankle braces for patients he never contacted, including deceased patients and amputees; Real Time sold the prescriptions to genetic testing labs and DME suppliers who billed Medicare over $3.2 million (paid over $1.3 million) and shared proceeds, with Becerril paid $20 per prescription totaling over $37,000. Sentencing figures span two defendants: Becerril awaits sentencing (convicted at trial), while Real Time owner Marc Sporn was previously sentenced to 14 years.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI has no E/M or telehealth claim with the beneficiary before the genetic test or brace order. Portal audit logs show order-signing intervals of seconds per record for a single ordering NPI. Dates of service postdate beneficiary death recorded in the Death Master File. Lower-limb brace L-codes are ordered for beneficiaries with prior amputation diagnosis codes in their claim history. One ordering NPI writes orders spanning many states and dozens of unrelated supplier and lab NPIs weekly.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the nearest E/M or telehealth claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists; action prepay edit. 2) Anatomic contradiction: on claim line, compute whether the ordered orthotic HCPCS body site matches a limb with a prior amputation diagnosis or amputation procedure in the beneficiary's claim history; fires on exact contradiction; action prepay edit. 3) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the distinct count of beneficiary states, supplier NPIs, and laboratory NPIs on signed orders; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Texas
FraudEntity: Samad Khan, M.D. (physician, owner of SK Primary Care, PLLC); SK Primary Care, PLLC
State_County: Texas - Collin County (Frisco); Texas (dozens of COVID-19 testing sites statewide)
PayerName: HRSA COVID-19 Claims Reimbursement to Health Care Providers and Facilities for Testing, Treatment, and Vaccine Administration for the Uninsured Program
FraudTypeAll: Upcoding; Phantom Claims; Covid or General Loan Fraud
SchemeSummary: At walk-up/drive-through COVID-19 test sites staffed by medical assistants, specimen collection (properly CPT 99211) was instead billed to the HRSA Uninsured Program as Level 2-5 evaluation and management office visits with Khan as sole rendering provider - approximately 400,000 claims from April 2020 to October 2021 - even though no physician or qualified health professional ever saw the patients; a second E/M 'encounter' was also billed for phoning or texting test results by staff who often never spoke to the patient.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, a single rendering NPI is attached to a volume of E/M claims that exceeds feasible encounter minutes per day. Level 3-5 E/M codes are billed on the same dates as specimen collection codes at temporary drive-through place-of-service settings. The distribution of E/M levels for the practice is nearly all high-level, an outlier versus same-specialty peers. Two E/M encounters are billed per beneficiary per test event, one on the collection date and one on the result date. Payroll and credentialing records show only medical assistants staffing the sites, with no supervising physician onsite documentation.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Rendering-NPI capacity: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total E/M typical-time minutes summed across all claim lines; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) E/M level distribution: on billing TIN x month, compute the share of E/M claim lines at levels 3 through 5 for COVID testing encounters; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension. 3) Duplicate result-call encounter: on beneficiary x testing episode, compute the count of E/M claim lines within the days following the specimen collection date; fires when a second E/M line exists without a documented separately identifiable service; action prepay edit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
FraudEntity: Hector Villegas-Alvarez
SchemeSummary: Not a health care fraud case: defendant was indicted for assaulting an ICE deportation officer while resisting arrest, causing a broken nose and concussion.
WaysToIdentify: This is an assault prosecution with no billed service, no payer, and no adjudication point. No claim, enrolment, or prior-authorisation signal exists to observe. The nearest route is law enforcement incident reporting, outside any payment system.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Handle through law enforcement incident reporting rather than claims analytics.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Missouri
FraudEntity: Jerry Joseph Bruggeman, M.D. (physician)
FraudTypeAll: Falsify certificate; kickback_Bribery For Referral; Device, DME; FakeEncounter
SchemeSummary: A telehealth company aggregated Medicare beneficiary information from marketing companies, generated assessments and orders, and paid Bruggeman roughly $29,440 to sign over 3,100 orders for cancer/pharmacogenetic testing and orthotic braces through an online portal without any patient contact; the resulting 8,700+ claims caused Medicare Part B to pay $1,055,303 for genetic testing and $551,105 for DME.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI has no prior E/M or telehealth claim with the beneficiary for the genetic test or brace order. Portal signing logs show hundreds of orders signed per session by one ordering NPI with negligible review time. The same ordering NPI supplies orders to many unrelated laboratory and supplier NPIs across widely dispersed states. Cancer and pharmacogenetic panel CPT codes are ordered without any oncology or medication-management diagnosis in the beneficiary's history. Payments from the telehealth aggregator to the signing physician appear as per-order fees in the entity's disclosed financial relationships.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between the order date and the nearest E/M or telehealth encounter claim with that beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Signing velocity: on ordering NPI x day, compute the count of signed orders divided by logged portal minutes; fires when orders per minute exceed a physically feasible review rate; action claim suspension. 3) Clinical indication mismatch: on claim line for hereditary cancer or pharmacogenetic panels, compute the presence of a supporting diagnosis or prescribed drug in the beneficiary's 12-month claim history; fires when none exists; action prior-authorisation requirement.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Louisiana
FraudEntity: Community Health Care Solutions, LLC (Shreveport counseling service); Estate of Yolanda Burnom (deceased owner/operator)
FraudTypeAll: Phantom Claims; kickback_Bribery For Referral; Falsify certificate; Upcoding; Wire Fraud
SchemeSummary: Community Health and its owner paid Medicaid recipients financial incentives to hand over their patient information, then billed Louisiana Medicaid for crisis intervention services (the highest-reimbursing code) that never occurred, with counselors instructed to cut-and-paste generic notes into patient files; many counselors never met the patients. The estate and company agreed to pay $4.6 million after Burnom died following a 2022 federal indictment.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, crisis intervention codes make up nearly all of the provider's billed behavioral health lines, an outlier versus peers. Crisis units per rendering counselor per day exceed feasible service minutes in a 24-hour period. Progress notes requested under ADR are byte-identical across unrelated beneficiaries in the same provider's records. Beneficiaries billed for crisis services have no emergency department, ambulance, or inpatient psychiatric claims around those dates. Beneficiary recruitment is suggested by many enrollees sharing a single address or referral source in the Medicaid eligibility file.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Crisis code concentration: on provider NPI x month, compute the share of behavioral health claim lines billed at the crisis intervention code and the paid dollars per beneficiary; fires when both are above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Counselor daily minutes: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of billed service units converted to minutes; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours or the scheduled shift length; action claim suspension. 3) Note duplication: on provider NPI, compute the pairwise text-similarity share among submitted progress notes across distinct beneficiaries; fires when the identical-note share is above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
FraudEntity: C&J Welding & Construction (subsidiary of Rema Tip Top of America, Inc.); Industrial Services Group, Inc. d/b/a Universal Blastco (subsidiary of Rema); NexGen Industrial Services, Inc. (subsidiary of Rema)
PayerName: Small Business Administration (U.S. government - Paycheck Protection Program)
FraudTypeAll: Covid or General Loan Fraud; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud
SchemeSummary: Three subsidiaries of Rema Tip Top of America applied for five PPP loans while knowingly failing to disclose their corporate affiliates, falsely certifying eligibility even though their combined employee counts/revenues exceeded PPP size limits; they received a total of about $8.85 million in loan forgiveness and interest (plus over $209,000 in lender processing fees paid by the U.S.) and paid $13 million to settle FCA claims brought by a qui tam relator, who received $2.34 million.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim here and no adjudication point, since the money moved as a forgivable SBA loan.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control is a pre-forgiveness affiliation check joining the applicant EIN to common-ownership and parent-subsidiary records in Dun & Bradstreet, SAM.gov and IRS EIN filings before forgiveness is granted.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas
FraudEntity: Nnwood Pharmacy; Cheryl Brew Greenleaf (owner); Wendell Kirk Greenleaf (owner)
SchemeSummary: Civil complaint alleges the pharmacy and its owners dispensed hydrocodone, carisoprodol and other Schedule II-IV controlled substances without legitimate medical purpose - filling prescriptions purportedly written by physicians hundreds of miles away, by OB/GYNs for male customers, and under invalid DEA registration numbers (99 allegedly fraudulent prescriptions seized during a 2021 inspection warrant) - and failed to keep required CSA records.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication the prescriber DEA number on the NDC claim fails validation against the DEA CSA registration file for that date. The prescriber NPI specialty in NPPES is obstetrics-gynecology while the beneficiary is male on the eligibility file. Distance between the prescriber practice address in PECOS and the dispensing pharmacy address exceeds any plausible care radius. The pharmacy's dispensed quantity of hydrocodone and carisoprodol per month far exceeds ARCOS purchase volume of same-size peers. The same beneficiary receives overlapping opioid and muscle-relaxant fills from a single pharmacy on repeated dates in PDMP data.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) DEA registration validity: on claim line, compare the prescriber DEA number and schedule authority against the DEA registration file on the fill date; fires on exact registry mismatch or expiry; action prepay edit. 2) Prescriber-patient geography: on beneficiary x pharmacy NPI, compute road miles between the prescriber PECOS practice address and pharmacy service address on controlled-substance fills; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension. 3) Specialty-drug incongruity: on prescriber NPI x NDC, compute the share of Schedule II-IV fills whose beneficiary sex or diagnosis is incompatible with the NPPES taxonomy; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of North Carolina
FraudEntity: Keke Komeko Johnson (Compliance Director, Life Touch LLC); Francine Sims Super (office manager, Life Touch LLC); Life Touch LLC
FraudTypeAll: kickback_Bribery For Referral; Tax, Payroll or Coupon Fraud; Falsify certificate
SchemeSummary: Leaders of a Kinston substance abuse treatment company used Medicaid reimbursement funds to buy more than $1 million in gift cards (sometimes routed through personal bank accounts) and handed them weekly to patients based on the number of days they attended, so Life Touch could bill Medicaid for more service days; Johnson lied to Medicaid auditors and Super created false documents, and both took unreported kickbacks from a drug-testing lab (1st Choice Healthcare Services) and failed to file tax returns.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, attendance-based service-day counts per beneficiary cluster tightly at the maximum billable days per week in the claim history. Cost-report and bank data show large gift-card and cash-equivalent purchases funded from Medicaid remittance deposits. Nearly every attending beneficiary also has definitive urine drug testing claims from one single referral laboratory TIN. Documentation produced to auditors shows identical group-note text across beneficiaries and dates of service. Provider enrollment on CMS-855 lists staff counts too small to support the billed daily census hours.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Attendance saturation: on beneficiary x provider NPI x month, compute billed service days as a fraction of maximum allowable days; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Lab referral concentration: on treatment provider NPI x quarter, compute the share of attending beneficiaries with definitive UDT claims billed by a single laboratory TIN; fires when concentration is above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action postpay audit. 3) Capacity-versus-census: on provider NPI x date of service, compute billed patient-hours divided by credentialed staff hours from the CMS-855 and payroll file; fires when the ratio implies more than 24 staff-hours per staff member per day; action payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Oklahoma
FraudEntity: Christopher R. Parks (compounding pharmacy owner)
SchemeSummary: Parks, a compounding pharmacy owner, was convicted in October 2023 of Conspiracy to Offer and Pay Health Care Kickbacks and sentenced to 18 months in prison with more than $6.4 million in restitution ordered. After release he paid only $8,450 toward restitution while concealing checking accounts and businesses through which over $560,000 was deposited and withdrawn (more than $320,000 in cash) between March 2024 and June 2025, and transferred assets to family; he was sentenced to an additional 15 months for violating supervised release.
WaysToIdentify: This case is post-conviction concealment of assets from restitution collection, so there is no claim and no adjudication point.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control is a monthly join of convicted-provider identifiers to OIG LEIE, PECOS ownership and payer bank-account records so any new TIN or bank account sharing the individual triggers payment offset.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Connecticut
FraudEntity: Lakshmi Bethi, DMD (dentist/owner); New Haven Dental LLC; New Haven Family Dental LLC; New Haven Family Dental Group LLC
PayerName: Medicaid (Connecticut Medical Assistance Program / Connecticut Dental Health Partnership)
SchemeSummary: Bethi and her dental practices paid a third-party patient recruiting company $110 per Connecticut Medicaid patient referred whenever that patient received services beyond routine preventive care, then billed CTMAP for those services while impliedly certifying no kickbacks were paid; she paid over $360,000 in kickbacks and Medicaid reimbursed about $2.2 million. The $608,296.39 civil settlement resolved FCA claims for 2019-2023 conduct, and in the related criminal case Bethi received two years' probation plus a $500,000 forfeiture.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, the share of the practice's Medicaid patients escalating from preventive codes to restorative or surgical codes exceeds peers. Practice bank and general-ledger records show recurring per-head payments to a marketing entity tracking new Medicaid patient counts. New beneficiaries arrive in geographic clusters far from the practice address on the CMS-855 enrollment file. Many new patients share the same referral source field and have no prior dental claim history with any local provider. The practice's new-patient volume steps up abruptly relative to its own trailing remittance baseline after a marketing contract begins.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Preventive-to-treatment conversion: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of beneficiaries with D2000-D7999 claims to beneficiaries with only D0100-D1999 claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 2) Recruiter cluster: on practice NPI x month, compute the count of new Medicaid beneficiaries whose residence ZIP lies outside the enrolled service area, divided by all new beneficiaries; fires when above the provider's trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Per-patient marketing spend: on TIN x quarter, compute vendor payments to marketing entities divided by count of new Medicaid beneficiaries billed; fires when the quotient approximates a fixed per-patient amount; action payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Connecticut
FraudEntity: Dent Plus Family Dentistry, PLLC (dissolved dental practice, Stamford); L&M Family Dentistry, LLC (dissolved dental practice, New Haven); Ivan Makar, DDS (owner); Oleg Losin, DDS (owner)
State_County: Connecticut - Stamford (Fairfield County); Connecticut - New Haven (New Haven County)
SchemeSummary: Two dental practices and their dentist owners paid a third-party patient recruiting company a per-patient fee for each Connecticut Medicaid patient referred to them, then billed the Connecticut Medical Assistance Program for dental services while impliedly certifying no kickbacks were paid, in violation of the CTDHP provider manual's ban on per-patient referral compensation; Makar and Losin jointly paid $714,446.27 to resolve federal and state False Claims Act allegations without admitting liability.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, new Medicaid patient arrivals per month step far above the practice's own trailing remittance baseline. Practice ledgers show payments to a recruiting vendor scaling linearly with counts of new Medicaid beneficiaries billed. Referred beneficiaries reside in ZIPs outside the service area declared on the CMS-855 enrollment record. Multiple unrelated dental TINs pay the same vendor and share overlapping referred-beneficiary rosters in claim history. Provider agreement attestations in the CTDHP provider manual bar per-patient compensation, which conflicts with the vendor invoices.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Shared-recruiter graph: on marketing vendor TIN, compute the count of distinct dental provider NPIs paying it and the count of beneficiaries appearing across their claims; fires when graph degree is above the calibrated percentile versus peer vendors; action postpay audit. 2) New-patient surge: on provider NPI x month, compute new Medicaid beneficiaries billed versus the provider's trailing twelve-month mean; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline by the calibrated multiple; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Out-of-area referral rate: on provider NPI x quarter, compute the share of billed beneficiaries whose ZIP falls outside the enrolled service area; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Connecticut
FraudEntity: Genco Lab, LLC (reference laboratory); Paul Conroy (majority owner); Tricia Conroy (Chief Operating Officer); Charles Orefice (part owner)
SchemeSummary: Genco Lab billed Medicare and Connecticut Medicaid for medically unnecessary urine drug tests, including tests done solely for 'residential monitoring' of sober-home residents (explicitly non-covered), and routinely billed both presumptive screening and the more expensive definitive confirmation test on the same patient the same day without any practitioner reviewing the screening result to justify the confirmatory test. The lab and its three owners/officers agreed to pay $1,255,825 collectively.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, presumptive codes 80305-80307 and definitive codes G0480-G0483 appear for the same beneficiary on the same date of service. The ordering NPI has no clinical encounter claim between the presumptive result date and the confirmatory order date. Definitive testing is billed at the highest analyte tier for nearly every beneficiary regardless of diagnosis. Beneficiary addresses concentrate at a small number of sober-home addresses in the eligibility file. Testing frequency per beneficiary per month exceeds treatment-plan intervals documented in prior-authorisation records.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Same-day reflex without review: on beneficiary x date of service, compute whether both a presumptive UDT code and a definitive UDT code are billed with no intervening practitioner E/M claim; fires when both present and gap is zero days; action prepay edit. 2) Tier uniformity: on laboratory NPI x quarter, compute the share of definitive UDT claims at the highest analyte tier; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Congregate-address density: on residence address x laboratory NPI, compute the distinct beneficiary count and monthly tests per beneficiary; fires when tests per beneficiary per month exceed the plan-documented interval; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
FraudEntity: Jesse Foote (controlled marketing company and DME suppliers)
FraudTypeAll: kickback_Bribery For Referral; Device, DME; FakeEncounter; Falsify certificate
SchemeSummary: Foote bought patient leads and pre-written doctors' orders for orthotic braces from overseas telemarketing call centers, paid kickbacks to telemedicine companies which bribed doctors to sign DME orders without patient contact or medical-necessity assessment, then sold the signed orders to DME suppliers (including his own) that billed Medicare, TRICARE and private insurers more than $7.8 million.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on L-code brace claims has no prior E/M encounter with that beneficiary. One telemedicine ordering NPI signs orders for beneficiaries across dozens of states within a single week. Beneficiary residence ZIPs fall far outside the service area on the supplier's CMS-855S enrollment record. The same beneficiary receives the same L-code brace from several unrelated supplier NPIs inside one month. Multiple supplier NPIs with different TINs share one billing agent identifier and one remittance bank account.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim linking that ordering NPI to the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute the count of distinct beneficiary states and distinct supplier NPIs on ordered DMEPOS claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Shared payee graph: on bank account, compute the count of distinct supplier NPIs and TINs receiving remittance; fires when that count exceeds one without disclosed common ownership in PECOS; action site visit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Connecticut
FraudEntity: Pain Management, LLC; Halina Snowball, M.D. (owner, physiatrist)
FraudTypeAll: Unbundling; Phantom Claims; Retention of Overpayment
SchemeSummary: Snowball and her pain management practice appended Modifier 25 to evaluation and management claims billed alongside pain injections to Medicare, claiming separately identifiable E&M services that were not actually provided; after being notified in November 2019 of improper Modifier 25 use and assessed an overpayment, they continued the improper billing until August 2023 and paid $427,129.11 to resolve liability.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, Modifier 25 appears on nearly every E/M line paired with a same-day injection procedure code. The provider's Modifier 25 rate exceeds the same-specialty peer distribution in the payer's claim history. The provider continued the same modifier pattern after a documented overpayment notice in the remittance and correspondence file. Submitted records show identical E/M note text and no separately identifiable problem beyond the injection indication. The beneficiary's other claims show no distinct diagnosis code supporting a separate evaluation on that date.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Modifier 25 intensity: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute Modifier 25 E/M lines divided by all E/M lines billed with a same-day procedure; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit. 2) Post-notice persistence: on provider NPI, compute the Modifier 25 rate in the 90 days after an overpayment notice versus the 90 days before; fires when the rate does not decline below the provider's own prior baseline; action payment suspension. 3) Diagnosis distinctness: on claim line, compute whether the E/M diagnosis code differs from the procedure diagnosis code on the same date; fires when the codes are identical on a Modifier 25 line; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Connecticut
FraudEntity: Mercer (US), LLC (consulting company/government contractor)
SchemeSummary: Mercer invoiced the Defense Health Agency monthly under a Blanket Purchase Agreement for Health Plan Innovative Support consulting services, billing the labor of 11 employees and subcontractor employees at higher hourly labor-category rates than their actual education and experience qualified them for; Mercer self-disclosed and paid $456,796.50 to resolve contract and unjust enrichment claims.
WaysToIdentify: At invoice adjudication, the named employee's degree and years of experience in the contract qualification file fail the labor-category minimums in the Blanket Purchase Agreement. Billed hourly rates for individual staff exceed the rate ceiling for the category their resume supports. Subcontractor staff appear on invoices without a qualification package on file for the billed category. Monthly invoices show the same employee billed under a higher category than in prior periods without any credential change.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Category qualification match: on invoice line x employee identifier, compare degree and experience years in the personnel qualification file against the BPA labor-category minimums; fires on exact mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Rate ceiling test: on invoice line, compute billed hourly rate minus the contract ceiling rate for the substantiated category; fires when the difference is positive; action claim suspension. 3) Category drift: on employee identifier x month, compute changes in billed labor category versus the prior invoice with no new credential record; fires when the category rises without a credential update; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Texas
FraudEntity: Trivikram Reddy (licensed nurse practitioner, owner of medical clinics); co-conspirators including two family members
PayerName: Medicare; Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas; Aetna; UnitedHealthcare; Humana; Cigna
FraudTypeAll: Phantom Claims; Wire Fraud; Falsify certificate; IdentityFraud
SchemeSummary: Reddy, a nurse practitioner, and co-conspirators submitted false patient bills to Medicare and five commercial insurers using the provider numbers of six doctors as the purported treating physicians, though none of those doctors provided billable services at his clinics; fake medical records were manufactured when federal agents inquired, and proceeds were laundered into nearly 200 bank accounts in India. Following his 2020 guilty plea, 2021 sentence of 20 years and over $50 million restitution order, a civil forfeiture judgment in March 2025 required return of up to $41,237,703.16 from the Indian accounts (stipulated by Reddy and two family members).
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, the rendering physician NPI's billed service hours across all sites exceed 24 hours per day. Listed physician NPIs have no payroll, credentialing or CMS-855 reassignment record tied to the billing TIN. Claims are billed from clinic addresses hundreds of miles from the physician's NPPES practice location on the same day. One billing TIN routes remittance to a large number of distinct bank accounts. Medical records supplied after an ADR were created after the request date per document metadata.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Reassignment registry match: on claim line, compare the rendering NPI to the CMS-855R reassignment and credentialing roster for the billing TIN on the date of service; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Physician time impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of CPT time-based service minutes across all TINs; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action payment suspension. 3) Payee fan-out: on billing TIN, compute the distinct count of remittance bank accounts and payee names over a rolling quarter; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action site visit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. District Court for the Western District of Wisconsin; U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Division, Consumer Protection Branch, with the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Wisconsin
FraudEntity: KBWB Operations LLC, d/b/a Atrium Health and Senior Living (nursing facility operator/owner); Kevin Breslin (former Chief Executive Officer, Managing Member and part owner)
State_County: Wisconsin; New Jersey - Little Falls (corporate headquarters); Wisconsin - Appleton (Midwest corporate office); Michigan
FraudTypeAll: Other - Unknown; Tax, Payroll or Coupon Fraud
SchemeSummary: Breslin and KBWB-Atrium, which operated 23 Wisconsin skilled nursing facilities funded primarily by Medicare and Medicaid, diverted CMS funds meant for facility operations and resident care to owner distributions, guaranteed payments and personal expenses, leaving vendors and third-party administrators unpaid (including employee insurance premiums and 401(k) withholdings); Breslin also directed that income and employment taxes withheld from employee paychecks not be paid to the IRS. Both defendants pleaded guilty to health care fraud and tax conspiracy and await sentencing.
WaysToIdentify: At cost-report review, reported direct resident-care spending per patient day falls far below the facility's Medicare and Medicaid revenue per patient day. Owner distributions and related-party payments in the Medicare cost report Worksheet S-2 and A-8-1 rise while vendor payables age. State survey and complaint files show unpaid vendors, staffing shortfalls and supply gaps across commonly owned facilities. Payroll-Based Journal staffing hours per resident day fall below the levels implied by billed acuity in MDS assessments. IRS payroll deposit records show withheld employment taxes never remitted for the same TIN.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Care-spend ratio: on facility CCN x cost-report year, compute direct resident-care expense divided by Medicare and Medicaid revenue; fires when below the calibrated percentile versus same-state peers; action postpay audit. 2) Related-party leakage: on owner TIN, compute the sum of distributions and related-party payments across all commonly owned CCNs in PECOS divided by total program revenue; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer chains; action payment suspension. 3) Staffing-versus-acuity gap: on facility CCN x quarter, compute Payroll-Based Journal nurse hours per resident day minus the hours implied by billed MDS case mix; fires when the gap is negative beyond the calibrated threshold; action site visit.
FeatureCategory: Cost Report and Risk Adjustment Audit

JurisdictionName: U.S. District Court for the Western District of Wisconsin; U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Wisconsin; Department of Justice Civil Division
FraudEntity: KBWB Operations LLC, d/b/a Atrium Health and Senior Living (operator/owner of skilled nursing facilities); Kevin Breslin (former chief executive officer and managing member)
State_County: Wisconsin; New Jersey - Little Falls (corporate headquarters); Wisconsin - Appleton (Midwest corporate office); Michigan
FraudTypeAll: Wire Fraud; Tax, Payroll or Coupon Fraud; Falsify certificate
SchemeSummary: KBWB-Atrium operated 23 Wisconsin skilled nursing facilities funded primarily by Medicare and Medicaid; Breslin diverted CMS funds intended for resident care to personal expenses and multi-million-dollar owner distributions, concealing from CMS that funds were not used for care and that vendors and taxes went unpaid, and also diverted employee health premiums, 401(k) contributions and resident account funds while directing that withheld employment taxes not be paid to the IRS. Restitution of $146 million and $8.4 million forfeiture were ordered against both Breslin and the corporation (same amounts, not cumulative).
WaysToIdentify: At cost-report review, direct care expense per resident day diverges sharply from program revenue per resident day across every facility in the chain. Worksheet A-8-1 related-party and owner-distribution amounts climb while Payroll-Based Journal hours fall. Vendor and third-party administrator complaints of nonpayment appear in state survey files for multiple commonly owned CCNs. Resident personal-needs account balances reported to the state do not reconcile with facility bank records. IRS records show withheld employment taxes and 401(k) remittances not deposited for the chain TIN.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Chain cash diversion: on owner TIN x quarter, compute owner distributions plus related-party transfers divided by Medicare and Medicaid remittance received across all CCNs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer chains; action payment suspension. 2) Payroll trust mismatch: on facility TIN x quarter, compute withheld employment tax and benefit amounts from payroll files minus amounts deposited per IRS and plan-administrator records; fires when the difference is positive; action claim suspension. 3) Resident fund reconciliation: on facility CCN x month, compute reported resident trust balances minus segregated bank account balances; fires when the difference is nonzero; action site visit.
FeatureCategory: Cost Report and Risk Adjustment Audit

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York
FraudEntity: Todd Faustin (current NYC Department of Correction officer); Jovanny Concepcion (former DOC correction officer); Steven Murphy (former DOC correction officer)
State_County: New York - Bronx County (Rikers Island, New York City)
PayerName: New York State Workers' Compensation Board (benefits paid from the New York City Treasury)
FraudTypeAll: Benefit & Eligibility Fraud; Phantom Claims; Wire Fraud
SchemeSummary: Three Rikers Island correction officers allegedly falsely claimed they were injured on duty during use-of-force incidents with incarcerated individuals, making false statements to the New York State Workers' Compensation Board, their own physicians, and independent medical examiners to obtain years of workers' compensation medical care and cash benefits paid from the New York City Treasury. Amounts span three defendants: Faustin $469,705.39, Concepcion $232,427.97, and Murphy $294,037.83; an attached later release states Faustin was sentenced to 15 months in prison.
WaysToIdentify: At claim adjudication, the incident report and use-of-force log for the claimed date contain no injury entry for that employee. Independent medical examiner findings contradict the treating physician's restriction letters in the workers' compensation file. Surveillance-equivalent evidence such as payroll, secondary-employment or activity records conflicts with total-disability certifications. Benefit duration for the claimed injury type exceeds the disability duration guideline for that body part. Multiple claimants from the same facility file similar injury claims naming the same treating physician.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Incident corroboration: on claim, compare the claimed injury date and mechanism against the employer incident and use-of-force log entries; fires on exact registry mismatch or absence; action claim suspension. 2) Duration outlier: on claimant x injury ICD code, compute paid indemnity weeks divided by the published disability duration guideline; fires when the ratio is above the calibrated percentile versus same-injury peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Treating-provider cluster: on treating physician NPI x employer, compute the count of distinct claimants certified totally disabled per quarter; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.
FeatureCategory: Coverage, Indication and Prior Auth Edits

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of California
FraudEntity: Luis Enrique Villegas Brownell; Kassandra Sanchez
State_County: California - San Diego County (San Diego/San Ysidro Port of Entry)
SchemeSummary: Villegas, a Mexican citizen without legal status, and his girlfriend Sanchez allegedly stole the identity documents of Sanchez's brother, used them to obtain a California DMV ID card bearing Villegas's photo, and used that fraudulent identity to cross the border more than 50 times, smuggle an undocumented immigrant, and fraudulently obtain California public benefits including Medi-Cal coverage.
WaysToIdentify: At eligibility determination, the applicant's submitted SSN and name fail SSA Numident verification against date of birth. Two active enrollment records share one SSN with different photographs and biometric identifiers in the state ID file. Claims are paid under the identity on dates when border-crossing or other government records place the true holder elsewhere. The enrollee's claim history shows a demographic profile inconsistent with prior claims under the same SSN.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Identity verification: on applicant record, compare submitted SSN, name and date of birth against SSA Numident and state DMV issuance records; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Duplicate identity: on SSN, compute the count of distinct enrollee records with differing photograph hashes or dates of birth; fires when that count exceeds one; action claim suspension. 3) Profile discontinuity: on beneficiary ID, compute the count of claim attributes such as sex, age and chronic diagnoses that change abruptly versus prior claim history; fires when changes exceed the calibrated threshold; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas
FraudEntity: Robert Maxwell (promoter/investment solicitor)
FraudTypeAll: Wire Fraud; Covid or General Loan Fraud
SchemeSummary: Maxwell solicited over $12.5 million from investors during the early COVID-19 pandemic by falsely claiming he had a Chinese manufacturing contract and a domestic sales agreement for PPE (masks, gloves) and was producing an at-home anti-coronavirus aerosol product with a Texas plant and out-of-state distributor; he used fabricated bank records, agreements and other documents and false claims of retailer sell-outs to obtain funds, then pocketed the money as no product ever existed.
WaysToIdentify: This is investor fraud over PPE supply contracts, so there is no health care claim and no adjudication point.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control is verification of purported manufacturing and distribution contracts and bank statements with the named counterparties and issuing banks before investor funds are transferred.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of California
SchemeSummary: Not a fraud case document: this is a press release announcing the swearing in of Craig H. Missakian as U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of California, which mentions only in passing his prior leadership of an investigation into a nationwide health care fraud scheme involving over $100 million in fraudulent Medicare claims, with no defendants or case details given.
WaysToIdentify: This document is an appointment announcement with no defendant, no claim and no adjudication point.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Florida
FraudEntity: Fernando Espinosa Leon (owner, Global Medical Supply Inc.); Global Medical Supply Inc.
SchemeSummary: Espinosa Leon used his company Global Medical Supply Inc. and stolen personally identifiable information of Medicare beneficiaries and medical practitioners to submit, through a third-party biller, more than $7.6 million in claims for durable medical equipment that was never prescribed or supplied; over $4 million was paid into a bank account he controlled.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, the ordering NPI on the DMEPOS claim has no prior encounter claim with the beneficiary. Beneficiaries billed by the supplier are geographically scattered far outside the CMS-855S service area. Ordering physician NPIs appear on claims after their NPPES records show retirement, relocation or death. Beneficiaries report no receipt and have no companion diagnosis claims supporting the billed HCPCS. All supplier remittances route to a single bank account tied to a third-party billing agent.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the nearest prior E/M claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Identity reuse velocity: on supplier NPI x week, compute the distinct count of ordering NPIs and beneficiary states on submitted DMEPOS claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) New-supplier ramp: on supplier NPI, compute weekly billed dollars versus its trailing baseline since PECOS enrollment approval; fires when the increase exceeds the calibrated percentile for newly enrolled suppliers; action site visit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
FraudEntity: Summit BHC New Jersey, LLC, d/b/a Seabrook (drug and alcohol rehabilitation facility)
PayerName: Veterans Health Administration Community Care Program; New Jersey Medicaid
FraudTypeAll: Falsify certificate; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud; FakeEncounter
SchemeSummary: Seabrook billed the VHA Community Care Program and New Jersey Medicaid for short-term residential treatment and partial hospitalization services for which it held no license or contract, concealed the unlicensed services from state inspectors, lacked sufficient properly credentialed staff, claimed to provide specialized veteran care that was identical to standard care, and kept false and inadequate treatment records. Resolved by a $19.75 million FCA settlement from a qui tam suit, with the relator receiving about $3,555,137.
WaysToIdentify: At credentialing, the facility holds no state licence for the residential or partial hospitalization level of care it bills. The revenue codes and HCPCS billed exceed the service categories authorised in the VA Community Care contract file. Rendering staff NPIs on claims lack the licensure required for the billed level of care in the state board file. Staffing ratios in payroll records fall below the licensure minimum for the billed daily census. Treatment records supplied on ADR lack individualised plans and signatures required for the billed level of care.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Licence-to-service match: on claim line, compare the billed level-of-care code against the facility's state licence categories and contract scope on the date of service; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Credentialed staff coverage: on facility NPI x date of service, compute billed patient-days divided by licensed clinician hours from payroll and state board files; fires when the ratio breaches the licensure minimum staffing ratio; action payment suspension. 3) Specialty-program premium: on facility NPI x quarter, compute the share of claims billed at the veteran-specialised rate whose records show identical content to standard-rate cases; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus contracted peers; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of California
FraudEntity: CVS Pharmacy Inc. (pharmacy chain)
SchemeSummary: CVS allegedly billed Medi-Cal for 'Code 1' formulary drugs without confirming or documenting the required approved diagnoses, and in some cases dispensed drugs for nonapproved diagnoses without submitting the required justification request to DHCS, then billed the program for those prescriptions. Resolved for $18,282,280 to the U.S. and California, with about $3.3 million to the whistleblower pharmacist.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, the restricted-formulary NDC is paid with no approved diagnosis code present on the claim or in the beneficiary's other claims. No treatment authorisation request appears in the DHCS prior-authorisation file for fills lacking an approved diagnosis. The dispensing pharmacy's rate of restricted-drug claims without diagnosis documentation exceeds chain peers. Diagnosis codes submitted on restricted-drug claims never appear in the beneficiary's medical claim history from any prescriber. Chain-level override or bypass codes are used at a rate above the pharmacy's own trailing baseline.
