Order signatures show identical timestamps in batches inconsistent with individual patient consultations in the laboratory requisition file. Multiple unrelated laboratory NPIs bill Medicare on orders bearing the same physician NPI within the same period.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Certification without encounter: on ordering NPI x beneficiary, compute the count of E/M claims between them in the lookback window before the order date; fires when zero; action prepay edit on the laboratory claim. 2) Signature throughput: on ordering NPI x day, compute the count of distinct genetic-test orders signed divided by available clinical hours; fires when implied minutes per order fall below a physically plausible consultation time; action payment suspension. 3) Orderer-to-lab fan-out: on ordering NPI x month, compute the distinct count of billing laboratory NPIs and beneficiary states on ordered genetic tests; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
FraudEntity: Rodrigo de Medeiros Siqueira (owner of Rodrigo Beauty Inc.); Rodrigo Beauty Inc.
SchemeSummary: Med spa owner, not licensed to prescribe, dispense or administer prescription drugs, allegedly injected clients with unapproved botulinum toxin obtained from illegitimate foreign sources while falsely representing himself as a licensed medical professional and misrepresenting the identity and source of the products; numerous clients developed botulism. Charged with misbranding a drug after shipment in interstate commerce with intent to defraud; agreed to plead guilty.
WaysToIdentify: There is no payer claim and no adjudication point, since the injections were cash-pay at an unenrolled med spa. The nearest detection route is the state licence board and medical spa registration file showing no prescriber licence at the business address. Wholesaler and import pedigree data show no lawful distribution of an FDA-approved botulinum toxin NDC to that facility. Public health botulism case reports linked to a single business address are the practical downstream signal.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest outside control: on facility address, compare state licence board prescriber records and DSCSA wholesaler pedigree shipments of botulinum toxin NDCs; fires when injections are advertised at an address with no licensed prescriber and no lawful product pedigree; action state board site visit and FDA import referral.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Virginia; U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, Norfolk Division
FraudEntity: Chesapeake Regional Medical Center (aka Chesapeake General Hospital, Chesapeake Regional Healthcare) (hospital); Dr. Javaid Perwaiz (physician with privileges at CRMC)
PayerName: Medicaid; health care benefit programs/insurance companies
SchemeSummary: CRMC was indicted for conspiracy and health care fraud for billing insurers and health care benefit programs for surgeries and procedures performed at its facility by Dr. Javaid Perwaiz, including medically unnecessary hysterectomies and other irreversible surgeries, elective inductions before 39 weeks without medical justification, and sterilizations of Medicaid patients lacking consent forms signed 30 days in advance; CRMC received about $18.5 million in reimbursements from 2010 to 2019 for Perwaiz's procedures. Perwaiz was separately convicted in November 2020 of 52 counts, about 38 involving procedures at CRMC.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, sterilisation claims lack a Medicaid consent form dated at least thirty days before the procedure date. One operating surgeon's hysterectomy rate per thousand attributed patients exceeds same-specialty peers at that facility. Elective induction claims carry gestational-age diagnosis codes below thirty-nine weeks without a documented medical indication. Preoperative pathology and imaging claims supporting the surgical indication are absent from the beneficiary's claim history. A single surgeon NPI accounts for an outsized share of the facility's inpatient gynaecologic surgical revenue.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Consent-form timing: on claim line for sterilisation procedures, compute days between the signed consent date and the date of service; fires when fewer than thirty days or no consent record exists; action prepay edit. 2) Surgeon procedure-rate outlier: on rendering NPI x facility x quarter, compute hysterectomies and other irreversible procedures per hundred attributed patients; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Indication support gap: on beneficiary x surgical claim, compute the count of supporting pathology, imaging or E/M claims in the preceding lookback window; fires when zero; action documentation request (ADR) then postpay audit of facility claims.
FeatureCategory: Coverage, Indication and Prior Auth Edits

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Delaware
FraudEntity: Ty Mauldin (medical biller and credentialer)
SchemeSummary: A medical biller/credentialer allegedly used the names and licensure information of medical professionals he worked with to order thousands of opioid pills from wholesale pharmaceutical suppliers and prescribe himself opioids; he also falsified his own electronic medical records and forged documents to pose as a cancer patient needing pain management (getting an intrathecal pain pump and opioids paid for by his private insurer), and falsely presented himself as a licensed nurse/certified medical assistant to perform Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation therapy on patients, billing Medicaid for it.
WaysToIdentify: Wholesaler and ARCOS pedigree data show controlled-substance orders shipped to a practice address under a licensee who never placed them. TMS therapy claims list a rendering identity with no active nurse or medical assistant credential in the state licence board file. The same person appears as beneficiary on opioid and pain-pump claims while acting as biller for the ordering practice. Prescriptions self-directed to a practice employee show prescriber and patient sharing an address in NPPES and eligibility records. Ordering volume for opioid NDCs at that practice exceeds its own trailing baseline without matching patient census growth.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Ordered-versus-dispensed drug reconciliation: on practice DEA registrant x month, compute wholesaler-shipped controlled-substance units minus units dispensed or administered on claims; fires when the unexplained surplus is above zero; action site visit. 2) Rendering-credential registry check: on claim line, compute an exact match of the rendering identity against the state licence board file for the credential required by the billed TMS CPT; fires on no active credential; action prepay edit. 3) Self-dealing overlap: on beneficiary identity, compute whether the same person appears as employee, biller or owner in the ordering practice's CMS-855 or payroll records; fires on any exact identity match with paid claims; action claim suspension and postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of New York
FraudEntity: Scott Newcombe (owner of SJ Healthcare Management Services, LLC; office manager and health care claims biller); SJ Healthcare Management Services, LLC
SchemeSummary: As office manager and billing agent for two Plattsburgh physicians' practices through his company SJHMS, Newcombe submitted false claims to public and private insurers for services never provided and for services billed at higher rates than actually delivered, including claims for procedures purportedly performed on himself that never occurred. He was sentenced to 1 year probation and $34,583.21 restitution.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, claims are submitted under a physician NPI naming the billing agent himself as the beneficiary. Billed E/M level distribution for the practice shifts to higher levels above the practice's own trailing baseline. Service dates fall on days the rendering physician had no other facility or office activity in claim history. The billing agent's TIN and pay-to bank account appear across multiple unrelated practice NPIs on remittance records. Claim volume per rendering NPI per day exceeds physically plausible encounter counts given billed time-based codes.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Biller-as-patient overlap: on claim line, compute an identity match between the beneficiary and any principal listed in the billing agent's TIN or the practice's CMS-855 contact fields; fires on exact match; action claim suspension. 2) Level-of-service drift: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the share of E/M claims at the two highest levels versus the provider's own trailing baseline and same-specialty peers; fires when above the calibrated percentile; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Rendering-day capacity: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute summed typical minutes for all billed time-based codes; fires when total exceeds a physically plausible workday; action prepay edit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Alabama
FraudEntity: Exactech, Inc. (medical device manufacturer, Gainesville, Florida)
PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid; U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
SchemeSummary: Exactech allegedly knew as early as January 2008 that its finned tibial tray, and as early as January 2019 that the polyethylene components in its Logic and Truliant knee systems, failed prematurely at higher-than-acceptable rates, yet continued marketing and selling them for total-knee replacements on Medicare, Medicaid and VA beneficiaries, causing false claims for devices that were not reasonable and necessary. Resolved for $8 million ($7.64M federal share, $360,000 state share) under the False Claims Act following two qui tam suits.
WaysToIdentify: In claim history, revision knee arthroplasty CPT codes cluster on beneficiaries whose implant model appears in device identifier fields. UDI device identifiers on implant claims map to catalogue numbers named in FDA recall and MAUDE adverse-event data. Time from index implant to revision for one manufacturer's device is shorter than for peer devices in longitudinal claims. Hospital-supplied implant charge lines continue after the manufacturer's own complaint files show elevated failure rates. Warranty and credit records show no manufacturer credit applied to the payer for premature device replacement.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Device survival outlier: on device identifier (UDI) x manufacturer, compute the median days from index implant claim to revision arthroplasty claim across beneficiaries; fires when materially below the same-procedure peer-device distribution; action postpay audit and False Claims Act referral. 2) Recall-registry match: on claim line, compute an exact match between the billed UDI or catalogue number and the FDA recall and safety-communication file; fires on any match after the recall effective date; action prepay edit. 3) Replacement credit reconciliation: on beneficiary x revision claim, compute the manufacturer credit amount posted against the implant charge; fires when the credit is zero for a device replaced inside its expected service life; action claim suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Michigan; U.S. District Court for the Western District of Michigan
FraudEntity: The Prometheus Group (medical device manufacturer); Richard Poore (president and sole owner)
SchemeSummary: A New Hampshire manufacturer of rectal therapeutic systems and its sole owner allegedly instructed health care providers to reuse FDA-cleared single-user rectal pressure sensors and single-use anorectal manometry catheters on multiple patients (covering probes with a glove or condom) to cut overhead costs; the resulting pelvic muscle rehabilitation services billed to Medicare were alleged to be not reasonable or necessary and thus false claims. Prometheus and Poore agreed to pay $550,000.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, anorectal manometry and biofeedback claims post without a matching billed single-use catheter or sensor supply line. Supply purchase volume from the manufacturer is far below the number of procedures billed by the same practice NPI. Procedures per catheter purchased exceed one, contradicting the FDA single-use labelling in the device 510(k) record. Manufacturer shipment and distributor pedigree data show declining probe orders while provider procedure volume rises. Practices trained by that manufacturer share the same anomalous supply-to-procedure ratio in remittance history.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Single-use supply reconciliation: on billing NPI x quarter, compute billed anorectal manometry and pelvic rehabilitation procedures divided by documented single-use catheter or sensor purchases from distributor records; fires when the ratio exceeds one per procedure; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Missing supply line: on claim line, compute whether the required single-use device HCPCS or supply charge appears on the same date of service for that beneficiary; fires when absent; action prepay edit. 3) Manufacturer-cluster ratio: on manufacturer customer list x provider NPI, compute the distinct count of NPIs with supply-to-procedure ratios above the calibrated percentile versus peers; fires when the cluster exceeds peer expectation; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Kentucky
FraudEntity: Pedro Reyes (owner of durable medical equipment businesses)
State_County: Kentucky - Hardin County (Elizabethtown); Kentucky - Jefferson County (Louisville)
SchemeSummary: Through multiple Kentucky companies, Reyes fraudulently billed Medicare for orthopedic durable medical equipment (back, knee and shoulder braces) that was medically unnecessary, unwanted by the patients, and never prescribed by their medical providers; he was sentenced to 33 months and ordered to pay $6,004,916 in restitution.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, orthotic L-code claims have no prior E/M encounter between the ordering NPI and the beneficiary. Ordering physicians deny signing when contacted, and their NPIs show no other DMEPOS ordering in claim history. One supplier's beneficiaries span states far outside the service area on its CMS-855S enrolment. The same beneficiary receives back, knee and shoulder braces on identical dates from one supplier NPI. Multiple supplier NPIs share an owner, address or bank account in CMS-855S ownership and remittance fields.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days between date of service and the most recent E/M claim between that orderer and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Multi-brace same-day bundle: on beneficiary x supplier NPI x date of service, compute the distinct count of orthotic L-code body regions billed; fires when the count exceeds the calibrated percentile versus peer suppliers; action claim suspension. 3) Common-control supplier cluster: on bank account and owner identity, compute the distinct count of enrolled supplier NPIs sharing it in CMS-855S; fires when greater than one with correlated billing spikes; action payment suspension and site visit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Kentucky
FraudEntity: Shafi Abbas (owner of Aidmen Medical Equipment LLC and Justright Medical Equipment LLC); Aidmen Medical Equipment LLC; Justright Medical Equipment LLC
SchemeSummary: Abbas, through his two DME companies, billed Medicare for durable medical equipment that was medically unnecessary, unwanted by the patients, and not prescribed by their medical providers, then transferred the fraud proceeds (over $10,000 per transaction) in money-laundering transactions.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, DMEPOS claims carry ordering NPIs with no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary. Beneficiary attestation and delivery-proof documents are absent or template-identical across the supplier's claims. The supplier's paid volume rises from near-zero to peer-top-decile within weeks of enrolment. Two supplier NPIs share an owner, address or pay-to bank account in CMS-855S ownership fields. Payments to that bank account are swept out in large transfers immediately after remittance posting.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the most recent E/M claim between orderer and beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists; action prepay edit. 2) New-supplier ramp: on supplier NPI x week, compute paid dollars versus the supplier's own trailing baseline since enrolment; fires when growth is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension pending site visit. 3) Shared bank account degree: on bank account, compute the distinct count of supplier NPIs receiving remittance plus days from deposit to outbound transfer; fires when multiple NPIs share the account with rapid sweep-out; action claim suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Virginia
FraudEntity: Fairfax Radiological Consultants, PLLC, formerly known as Fairfax Radiological Consultants, P.C. (radiology medical group)
PayerName: Small Business Administration - Paycheck Protection Program
FraudTypeAll: Covid or General Loan Fraud; Tax, Payroll or Coupon Fraud
SchemeSummary: Radiology group obtained a $6.8 million PPP loan in April 2020 based on its 2019 payroll of over 500 employees when it actually employed fewer than 100, then in April 2021 falsely represented eligible payroll costs for 98 employees in its forgiveness application to obtain full forgiveness, though it was only entitled to $4,945,860.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health-care claim and no adjudication point, because the money came from an SBA loan programme, not billing. The nearest detection route compares the employee count and payroll certified on the PPP application against IRS Form 941 filings and state wage records. A second route compares the applicant's certified payroll against the payroll implied by its Medicare cost report or credentialed staff roster. Forgiveness applications listing far fewer employees than the loan application are checkable within SBA's own file.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest outside control: on borrower EIN, compute certified PPP payroll and headcount minus IRS Form 941 reported wages and employee counts for the same quarters; fires when the certified figure exceeds filed wages; action forgiveness denial and SBA Office of Inspector General referral.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
FraudEntity: PenRad Technologies, Inc. (medical software company headquartered in Raleigh, N.C.)
SchemeSummary: PenRad's Series 7 software sometimes installed the Tyrer-Cusick breast cancer risk calculator with 'competing mortality' disabled without telling customers, producing inflated patient risk scores; at least one provider consequently ordered medically unnecessary breast MRIs that were billed to Medicare and MassHealth, making PenRad liable under the False Claims Act for causing false claims (resolved for $529,069 following a qui tam suit).
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, screening breast MRI CPT claims cluster at practices using one risk-calculator software version. Ordered breast MRI rates per thousand screened women exceed same-specialty peers for those ordering NPIs. Documented lifetime risk scores in prior-authorisation records exceed scores recomputed from the same patient inputs. Beneficiaries lack genetic-mutation or high-risk diagnosis codes that normally accompany supplemental MRI in claim history. The elevated ordering pattern starts sharply at a software installation date recorded in vendor deployment files.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Risk-score recomputation: on prior-authorisation record, compute the difference between the submitted lifetime risk score and the score recomputed from the submitted Tyrer-Cuzick inputs; fires when the difference exceeds tolerance; action prepay edit. 2) MRI ordering rate: on ordering NPI x quarter, compute supplemental breast MRI orders divided by screening mammograms for the same panel; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Indication support: on beneficiary x MRI claim, compute the count of high-risk diagnosis or genetic-mutation codes in the preceding claim history; fires when zero and risk score is the sole justification; action documentation request (ADR).
FeatureCategory: Coverage, Indication and Prior Auth Edits

JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Division and U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of California
FraudEntity: Seoul Medical Group Inc. (Medicare Advantage provider); Advanced Medical Management Inc. (subsidiary); Dr. Min Young Cha (former president and majority owner); Renaissance Imaging Medical Associates Inc. (radiology group)
SchemeSummary: Seoul Medical Group and its owner allegedly submitted diagnosis codes for two severe spinal conditions (spinal enthesopathy and sacroiliitis) for patients who did not have them, inflating beneficiaries' risk scores so CMS paid Medicare Advantage plans more, with the plans passing a portion of the increased payment to Seoul; when an MA Plan questioned the enthesopathy coding, Renaissance Imaging created radiology reports appearing to support the diagnosis. Settlement totals $62.85M across defendants ($58,740,000 by Seoul/Advanced Medical Management, $1,760,000 by Dr. Cha, $2,350,000 by Renaissance Imaging).
WaysToIdentify: At encounter data validation, compute the share of a group's members carrying M46.0 spinal enthesopathy or M46.1 sacroiliitis diagnoses versus same-region peers. Check whether each risk-adjusting diagnosis has any corresponding treatment, imaging or referral claim in the member's other claims history. Look for enthesopathy and sacroiliitis codes appearing only on addenda or chart-review submissions with no linked professional encounter claim. Compare radiology report dates in the imaging supplier's records against the date the MA plan queried the diagnosis, indicating back-dated reports. Track members whose HCC risk score jumps on capitation renewal without any new utilization in the payer's remittance history.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Orphan HCC diagnosis rate: on rendering NPI x diagnosis code, compute the fraction of members with M46.0 or M46.1 having no follow-on treatment, imaging or specialist claim within the year; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit of encounter data. 2) Chart-review-only additions: on provider group TIN x member, compute the count of risk-adjusting diagnoses submitted solely through supplemental chart review with no matching encounter claim line; fires when above the group's own trailing baseline; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Retro report creation: on imaging NPI x member, compute the gap in days between date of service and report authorship timestamp in the submitted record; fires when the gap exceeds the report-signature window in the plan's credentialing policy; action claim suspension.
FeatureCategory: Cost Report and Risk Adjustment Audit

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Tennessee
FraudEntity: Dr. Mark Shermer (Memphis nephrologist)
SchemeSummary: A Memphis nephrologist allegedly billed Medicare for end-stage renal disease treatment visits to dialysis patients that he never actually performed; the allegations were raised in a qui tam False Claims Act suit and resolved for $375,296.90 without a determination of liability.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compare monthly capitation ESRD MCP codes 90957-90962 against the dialysis facility's own treatment records for the same beneficiary dates. Compute daily face-to-face visit counts per rendering NPI across all dialysis facilities billed that day. Compare travel distance between dialysis facility addresses billed by one physician on one date of service. Check whether the physician's MCP claims continue during periods the beneficiary shows inpatient or hospice claims elsewhere. Compare the ratio of billed visits per ESRD patient month against same-specialty nephrology peers in remittance history.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Physician-day dialysis visit load: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct ESRD beneficiaries with face-to-face visit codes multiplied by minimum visit minutes; fires when the product exceeds 24 hours in a day; action prepay edit. 2) Facility cross-check: on beneficiary x month, compute the count of MCP visit tiers billed versus dialysis facility 72x claims documenting physician presence; fires when the billed tier exceeds documented visits; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Site dispersion: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct dialysis facility service addresses billed; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus nephrology peers; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Tennessee
FraudEntity: Nakita Cannady (owner and operator of What About Us In-Home Healthcare)
FraudTypeAll: Upcoding; Covid or General Loan Fraud
SchemeSummary: Cannady billed Cigna for 24 hours a day of in-home custodial care for mostly elderly patients when they had actually received only 8 or 12 hours a day, and separately submitted six PPP/EIDL applications for four businesses she controlled containing false dates of operation, revenues, employee counts and payroll figures; restitution totaled $193,508.10 to Cigna and $346,882.13 to the SBA.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, sum billed custodial care hours per beneficiary per calendar day across all claim lines from the agency. Compare billed hours against EVV clock-in and clock-out records and caregiver timesheets for the same dates. Compute per-caregiver daily hours across all beneficiaries served by the agency NPI. Check whether authorized hours on the plan's prior-authorization record match units billed per date of service. Compare the agency's payroll totals against total billed service hours for the same period.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Round-the-clock billing: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the sum of custodial care units converted to hours across all claim lines; fires when the sum exceeds authorized hours on the prior-authorization record or exceeds 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) EVV-to-claim variance: on beneficiary x supplier NPI x week, compute billed hours minus EVV-verified visit minutes; fires when the variance exceeds zero for any day; action claim suspension. 3) Payroll coverage ratio: on provider NPI x month, compute total billed care hours divided by paid caregiver hours from payroll records; fires when the ratio is above one; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida
FraudEntity: Manuel Delgado (contractor/inspector for Board of Certification/Accreditation, International)
FraudTypeAll: kickback_Bribery For Referral; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud; Device, DME
SchemeSummary: Delgado, a contractor performing CMS quality-standard accreditation inspections of DME companies for BOC, took cash bribes from DME company owners to expedite accreditation so they could enroll and bill Medicare, and also formed DME companies in family members' names, inspected and accredited them himself, then sold them as Medicare-enrolled suppliers; the accredited companies were valued at over $1.4 million.
WaysToIdentify: At enrolment, match accreditation inspector identity against the CMS-855S owner, officer and managing-employee names for surname and address overlap. Compare the inspector's inspection date log against site-visit travel feasibility, counting distinct site addresses inspected per day. Check newly accredited supplier NPIs whose PECOS ownership changes hands within months of accreditation. Compare the enrolment address against other supplier NPIs sharing the same suite, phone and bank account. Compare time from accreditation application to award against the accreditor's own trailing baseline for that inspector.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Inspector-owner kinship overlap: on supplier NPI, compute the count of exact matches between accrediting inspector name or address and CMS-855S owner, officer and managing-employee fields; fires when any exact registry match exists; action site visit before enrolment approval. 2) Inspection throughput: on inspector ID x date, compute the count of distinct supplier site addresses accredited; fires when count multiplied by minimum inspection duration exceeds an eight-hour workday; action claim suspension for suppliers in that batch. 3) Flip-after-accreditation: on supplier NPI, compute the gap in days between accreditation date and first PECOS ownership change; fires when the gap is below the calibrated percentile versus peers; action prior-authorisation requirement on all billing.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section (National Rapid Response Strike Force)
FraudEntity: Sophie Toya, M.D. (physician who signed orthotic brace prescriptions)
FraudTypeAll: Device, DME; Falsify certificate; kickback_Bribery For Referral; FakeEncounter
SchemeSummary: Patients recruited through deceptive TV ads for 'free' back braces were routed to telemedicine companies; Toya signed over 7,900 orthotic brace prescriptions for more than 2,600 Medicare beneficiaries after minute-long calls or no contact at all, falsely attesting medical necessity, diagnoses and plans of care. Brace supply companies used the prescriptions to bill Medicare over $6.3 million, and Toya was paid about $120,000 by the telemedicine companies for signing.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, count orthotic brace orders signed per ordering NPI per day against the number of billable telehealth minutes that NPI billed. Check whether any E/M or telehealth claim exists between the ordering NPI and the beneficiary before the L-code date of service. Compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct supplier NPIs served by one ordering physician per week. Compare the ordering physician's state licence file against the beneficiary's state of residence in the eligibility record. Count distinct L-code braces per beneficiary within a rolling month across unrelated supplier NPIs.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Signature throughput: on ordering NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct DMEPOS orders signed divided by documented encounter minutes; fires when implied consult time per order falls below the minimum for a physical impossibility of 24 hours; action prepay edit. 2) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the most recent E/M or telehealth claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no such encounter exists in the lookback window; action claim suspension. 3) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct billing supplier NPIs on ordered L-code claims; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section; Eastern District of Michigan
FraudEntity: Nabil Fakih (pharmacist, pharmacy owner/operator)
SchemeSummary: Fakih billed Medicare for high-reimbursing prescription drugs (blood thinners, lung disease inhalers) that his Dearborn Heights pharmacy never dispensed and lacked the inventory to dispense, concealing the scheme by manipulating inventory purchase records and diverting proceeds for personal use; ordered to pay $4M restitution plus $726,364.96 and four properties forfeited.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compare NDC-level dispensed quantities against wholesaler acquisition pedigree and ARCOS purchase data for the same pharmacy NPI. Compute the ratio of billed units of high-cost anticoagulants and inhalers to total prescription volume versus same-size pharmacy peers. Check whether the prescribing NPI on each claim has any office-visit claim with that beneficiary in the relevant period. Look for beneficiaries with no refill-adherence pattern yet continuous costly fills in remittance history. Compare pharmacy purchase invoices submitted at revalidation against total billed dispense quantity per NDC.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Inventory reconciliation: on pharmacy NPI x NDC x quarter, compute billed dispensed units minus wholesaler-documented acquired units; fires when billed exceeds acquired; action payment suspension. 2) High-cost NDC concentration: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of paid dollars from top-decile-cost NDCs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-region pharmacy peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Prescriber linkage: on claim line, compute days between fill date and nearest E/M claim between prescriber NPI and beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists within the lookback window; action prepay edit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Florida
FraudEntity: Walgreens Boots Alliance (pharmacy chain); Dr. Edward Lubin (pain management physician); Bluestone Physician Services (geriatric provider); Daniel Hurt (owner of Fountain Health Services LLC, Verify Health, Landmark Diagnostics LLC, First Choice Laboratory LLC, Sonoran Desert Pathology Associates LLC); Robert J. Remington and New Horizons Computer Learning Center franchises (Jacksonville and Orlando); Miles Partnership, LLC; H. Lee Moffitt Cancer and Research Center; Baptist Health System
Service: Pharmacy; PhysicianPractice; GeneticTesting; Laboratory; Hospital; Telehealth
State_County: Florida - Hillsborough County (Tampa); Florida - Duval County (Jacksonville); Florida - Orange County (Orlando)
PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid; other federal health care programs; Department of Veterans Affairs (Post-9/11 GI Bill); Small Business Administration (PPP)
FraudTypeAll: Phantom Claims; kickback_Bribery For Referral; Upcoding; Drug_Prescriptions; FakeEncounter; Covid or General Loan Fraud
SchemeSummary: Annual MDFL collections release summarizing multiple resolutions: Walgreens billed Medicare/Medicaid $106.8M worth of prescriptions that were processed but never picked up by beneficiaries (2009-2020); Dr. Edward Lubin took Insys speaker-program kickbacks to prescribe the opioid Subsys ($1.5M); Bluestone Physician Services billed unnecessary or upcoded monthly visits to assisted-living residents ($14.9M); Daniel Hurt used telemarketers and telemedicine prescribers to generate medically unnecessary cancer genomic tests billed to Medicare through his labs and a hospital, paying kickbacks (~$27M, plus criminal guilty plea); Moffitt Cancer Center billed federal programs for clinical-trial items that should have been billed to trial sponsors ($19.56M); Baptist Health offered patient discounts as inducements ($1.5M); non-health-care matters included a New Horizons GI Bill subsidy case ($1.35M) and a Miles Partnership PPP second-draw loan obtained despite FARA ineligibility ($2.28M). Figures span multiple defendants.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compare pharmacy adjudicated claims against point-of-sale pickup records to find scripts billed but never removed from will-call inventory and never reversed. Count opioid claims per prescriber NPI cross-referenced with manufacturer Open Payments speaker-fee records for the same drug. Compute monthly E/M visit levels per assisted-living facility resident per rendering NPI versus peer distributions. Check genomic test claims for an ordering NPI with no prior treating relationship in the beneficiary's claim history. Match hospital claim lines against ClinicalTrials.gov trial numbers and sponsor-funded item lists in the Medicare Advantage secondary payer file.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Unclaimed prescription reversal: on pharmacy NPI x claim line, compute days between adjudication date and dispensing pickup timestamp; fires when no pickup is recorded past the return-to-stock window without a reversal; action prepay edit and postpay audit. 2) Speaker-payment-linked prescribing: on prescriber NPI x drug NDC, compute paid claim volume divided by trailing baseline, joined to Open Payments speaker fees from that manufacturer; fires when both volume and payments exceed the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Facility visit intensity: on rendering NPI x facility x month, compute visits per resident and the share coded at the two highest E/M levels; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers serving assisted living; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
FraudEntity: Mohammed Rahman (controlled Caltech Trading Corporation); Caltech Trading Corporation
SchemeSummary: Rahman, through Caltech Trading Corporation, induced about 60 South Korean victims to invest toward a purported $1 million purchase of Brazilian sugar under a fraudulent agreement promising a 100 percent return; instead the wired funds went into his personal bank account for expenses including his mortgage, and he altered bank statements to conceal it.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point in this investment scheme. Detection sits with bank anti-money-laundering monitoring of corporate accounts receiving pooled foreign investor wires. Securities regulators can match the entity against broker-dealer and commodity-trading registrations for unregistered offerings. Altered bank statements shown to investors are detectable by direct confirmation with the depository institution.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control: bank transaction monitoring on the business account, computing the count of inbound international wires from unrelated individuals followed by same-week transfers to the owner's personal account and mortgage servicer, escalated as a SAR.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
FraudEntity: Mohammed Rahman (controller of Caltech Trading Corporation); Caltech Trading Corporation
SchemeSummary: Rahman, through Caltech Trading Corporation, and associates in South Korea induced roughly 60 South Korean victims to invest in a purported $1 million purchase of Brazilian sugar under a fraudulent agreement promising a 100% return; the funds were instead wired to Rahman's personal bank account and spent on personal expenses including his mortgage, with bank statements altered to conceal the diversion. Restitution of $1,393,200 and forfeiture of $1,000,000 were ordered.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point in this commodity investment fraud. The nearest detection route is bank AML review of a trading company account funded by dozens of small foreign investor wires. Registration checks against commodity-broker and state securities registries would show no authority to solicit these investments.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control: on business bank account x month, compute the count of distinct inbound remitters and the ratio of funds transferred to the owner's personal account, escalating to a SAR when personal transfers dominate deposits.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Connecticut
FraudEntity: Ramon Apellaniz (a/k/a 'Kristopher Rockefeller', de facto operator of Minds Cornerstone under pseudonym; former operator of The Gemini Project, LLC); Suhail Aponte (sole principal and registered agent of Minds Cornerstone LLC); Minds Cornerstone LLC dba Minds Cornerstone Behavior Therapy Services
PayerName: Medicaid (Connecticut Medical Assistance Program / HUSKY, Connecticut Department of Social Services)
FraudTypeAll: Phantom Claims; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud; Falsify certificate; Unbundling
SchemeSummary: Apellaniz, an unlicensed provider running Minds Cornerstone under a pseudonym (including while incarcerated) with owner Aponte, billed Connecticut Medicaid roughly $1.88 million for applied behavior analysis services to autistic children that were never rendered - services for which payroll shows no employee was paid, BCBA supervision billed without the corresponding technician code, and services purportedly given to patients who were actually inpatient in a hospital. Apellaniz had earlier been convicted in state court for a similar $909,268 scheme through The Gemini Project and used Minds Cornerstone funds to pay part of that restitution; both defendants pleaded guilty federally and agreed to forfeit about $469,000 plus bank accounts and two Hartford land parcels.
WaysToIdentify: At enrolment and credentialing, match the rendering provider name against the state BCBA licence board file and OIG LEIE for exclusion or absence of licensure. Compare billed ABA technician units against the agency's payroll records for any paid employee on those dates of service. Check for BCBA supervision code 97155 billed on dates with no corresponding 97153 technician code for the same beneficiary. Cross-check ABA dates of service against the beneficiary's inpatient hospital claims for overlapping days. Compare enrolled owner and officer names on the Medicaid provider agreement against prior state fraud convictions and pseudonym aliases.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Licence and exclusion match: on rendering NPI x claim line, compute exact-match status against the state behavior-analyst licence file and OIG LEIE on the date of service; fires on any registry mismatch or exclusion hit; action prepay edit. 2) Supervision without service: on beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of 97155 supervision units where the count of 97153 technician units is zero; fires when greater than zero; action claim suspension. 3) Inpatient overlap: on beneficiary x date of service, compute overlapping minutes between billed outpatient ABA units and any inpatient facility stay span; fires when overlap exceeds zero; action prepay edit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Connecticut
FraudEntity: Habroon Habib (owner/formed company); Around the World Solutions LLC
FraudTypeAll: Phantom Claims; Device, DME; Wire Fraud
SchemeSummary: Habib formed Around the World Solutions LLC at a shared office space in Middletown and billed Medicare Advantage plan sponsors for orthotics purportedly supplied to more than 400 Medicare beneficiaries nationwide who never requested or received them; approximately $680,000 in plan checks were deposited into the company account and $425,000 was wired out to financial institutions in Pakistan.
WaysToIdentify: At enrolment, compare the supplier's CMS-855S practice location against shared virtual-office addresses used by other supplier NPIs. At adjudication, measure the distance between beneficiary residence ZIPs and the supplier's stated service area for nationwide orthotic billing. Check whether each L-code claim has an ordering NPI with any prior encounter claim for that beneficiary. Compare the supplier's payment bank account against outbound international wire activity flagged in the plan's vendor banking file. Compute time from first enrolment approval to peak billing volume against same-specialty supplier baselines.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) New-supplier velocity: on supplier NPI x week, compute paid orthotic claim dollars divided by weeks since PECOS enrolment approval; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus newly enrolled DMEPOS peers; action payment suspension pending site visit. 2) Geographic dispersion: on supplier NPI x month, compute the count of distinct beneficiary states and mean beneficiary-to-supplier distance; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action prepay edit. 3) Address and account sharing: on supplier NPI, compute the count of other supplier NPIs sharing the same 855S location, phone or payee bank account; fires when count exceeds zero without disclosed common ownership; action site visit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Ohio
FraudEntity: Neuro Stat Analytical Solutions, LLC (Neurostat) (Texas-based Air Force contractor)
PayerName: United States Air Force / Department of Defense (Defense Health Agency)
SchemeSummary: Neurostat, which contracted with the Air Force to develop and implement psychological assessments and occupational health stress screening tools, allegedly paid more than $1 million to a federal employee between 2016 and 2021 in exchange for preferential treatment on federal contracts awarded to or performed by the company; it agreed to pay $1.2 million to resolve False Claims Act allegations and to cooperate in the ongoing investigation of individuals.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim adjudication point; this is contract procurement bribery on a federal services contract. Detection sits with contracting-officer conflict screening comparing vendor payment ledgers against government employee financial disclosure filings. Contract award pattern analysis can show one contracting official repeatedly steering awards or modifications to a single vendor.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control: on contracting official x vendor, compute the count and dollar share of awards and modifications approved plus any match between vendor disbursement payees and the official's OGE-278 disclosed income sources, referred to the Inspector General when a match exists.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Minnesota
FraudEntity: Gabriel Adam Alexander Luthor, a.k.a. Gabriel Adam Alexander Langford (co-founder of Golden Victory Medical, LLC); Elizabeth Christine Brown (co-founder of Golden Victory Medical, LLC); Golden Victory Medical, LLC
SchemeSummary: Through Golden Victory Medical, LLC, the couple allegedly billed Medicare, Medicaid and private insurers for neurofeedback therapy using inapplicable CPT codes, code combinations that cannot be billed together, and codes reflecting longer service durations than actually provided, continuing after warnings from insurers, an auditor, and CMS; proceeds (~$15M loss) were moved between bank accounts and used to buy an Eden Prairie mansion and pay living expenses.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, run NCCI procedure-to-procedure edits on neurofeedback claim lines for mutually exclusive code pairs billed on the same date of service. Compute total timed-code minutes billed per rendering NPI per day from time-based CPT units. Compare the practice's code mix against same-specialty peers for use of codes inapplicable to neurofeedback. Check whether billing behavior changed after prior payer audit findings recorded in the payer's remittance and overpayment history. Compare billed service duration units against session logs and appointment schedules in requested documentation.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Mutually exclusive pairing: on claim line pair per beneficiary x date of service, compute the count of NCCI PTP-conflicting neurofeedback code combinations without a valid modifier; fires when count exceeds zero; action prepay edit. 2) Timed-unit day load: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of time-based CPT units multiplied by their defined minutes; fires when the total exceeds a 24-hour day or the clinic's staffed hours; action claim suspension. 3) Post-audit persistence: on provider TIN x month, compute the rate of previously denied or audited code combinations resubmitted after the audit notice date; fires when the rate exceeds zero above the provider's own trailing baseline; action payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Minnesota
FraudEntity: Tammy Wadsworth (founder and owner of Pain, Injury and Brain Centers of America); Pain, Injury and Brain Centers of America (PIBCOA)
SchemeSummary: Wadsworth founded PIBCOA and sold franchises (charging owners $60,000-$250,000 plus royalties and equipment costs) for clinics offering purported 'A.I. Myoneurvascular Therapy,' falsely claiming low-voltage electrode treatment could cure Alzheimer's, autism and other conditions with a 95% success rate; the devices she sold franchisees were relabeled with PIBCOA labels after manufacturer serial numbers and product information were removed, and she laundered proceeds into real estate and a Mercedes. Loss to franchise owners was $887,061 actual and more than $2 million total.
WaysToIdentify: There is generally no payer claim here because franchise buyers and cash patients, not insurers, funded the scheme. If clinics did bill, look for unlisted or miscellaneous electrical stimulation HCPCS codes tied to Alzheimer's and autism diagnoses lacking FDA-cleared indications. Device labels with removed manufacturer serial numbers are detectable through FDA UDI registry lookup at supplier accreditation. Franchise marketing claiming a 95 percent cure rate is actionable through FTC and state consumer-protection complaint records.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control: on supplier NPI x HCPCS, compute the count of claims for electrical stimulation devices whose UDI or serial number fails to match an FDA-registered manufacturer record, denying at prepay edit and referring to FDA.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section; U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Mississippi
FraudEntity: Willie De Gibbs (owner/beneficial owner of seven DME supply companies)
FraudTypeAll: Device, DME; kickback_Bribery For Referral; FakeEncounter; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud
SchemeSummary: Gibbs paid kickbacks for fraudulent doctors' orders and used them to bill Medicare over $19 million for medically unnecessary orthotic braces for beneficiaries who did not request or need them, submitting claims through seven DME supply companies, four of which he controlled through straw owners.
WaysToIdentify: At enrolment, compare CMS-855S owner, officer and managing-employee fields across supplier NPIs for shared addresses, phones and payee bank accounts revealing common control by straw owners. At adjudication, check whether the ordering NPI on each L-code claim has any prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary. Compute the count of distinct supplier NPIs billing braces for the same beneficiary within a rolling month. Compare a single ordering NPI's order volume and beneficiary state dispersion against same-specialty peers. Compare each supplier's brace claim volume against the number of documented beneficiary contacts in submitted records.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Common-control graph: on payee bank account and 855S address, compute the count of distinct supplier NPIs sharing that node in PECOS; fires when count exceeds one without disclosed common ownership; action prior-authorisation requirement across the linked NPIs. 2) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the nearest E/M claim between that NPI and beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 3) Beneficiary brace saturation: on beneficiary x L-code, compute the count of distinct supplier NPIs paid within rolling 30 days; fires when count exceeds one without a documented replacement reason; action claim suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Mississippi
FraudEntity: Rajwinder Kaur; Kawaldeep Singh; Narinder Kaur; Prabhdeep Momi; Bobby Babber; Priyalpreet Babber; Gurinder Babber; Mehaknoor Babber; Navdeep Basra (former Medicaid recipients; officers/registered agents/members/owners of convenience stores, gas stations, liquor stores, restaurants and other businesses)
SchemeSummary: The settling former Medicaid recipients, who owned or were officers of convenience stores, gas stations, liquor stores and restaurants, allegedly understated their household earned income on Mississippi Medicaid applications and renewals to create eligibility for their dependents, causing the state Medicaid agency to pay health coverage benefits they were not entitled to; the nine defendants collectively agreed to pay $173,627.
WaysToIdentify: There is a payer, but the fraud sits in eligibility determination rather than in a provider claim, so no adjudication edit catches it. The decisive check is at application and renewal: match self-reported household income against state wage-reporting and Department of Revenue business income files. Business ownership filings with the Secretary of State identify applicants who are officers of retail businesses while reporting minimal earnings. Federal data hub and IRS income verification at renewal would surface the same discrepancy.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control: on Medicaid applicant household, compute reported earned income minus wage and business income reported to the state revenue and Secretary of State files, referring for eligibility redetermination when the difference exceeds the program's reasonable-compatibility threshold.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
FraudEntity: Deer Valley Home Health Services LLC (DVHH) (home health care company); unnamed contractor/employee (purported applied behavior analysis provider)
SchemeSummary: A home health company billed Missouri Medicaid for applied behavior analysis therapy, assessments and treatment plans purportedly rendered by a contractor-turned-employee who had inflated his educational credentials and was not qualified to provide the services, and who also billed more than 24 hours of service in a single day; the company agreed to repay $534,475.
WaysToIdentify: At credentialing, verify the rendering provider's degree and BCBA certification directly against the BACB registry and state licence board file rather than the employer's attestation. At adjudication, sum all timed ABA units billed under one rendering NPI per date of service across beneficiaries. Compare the assessment and treatment-plan CPT codes billed against the credential level required by the state Medicaid provider manual. Check whether the rendering NPI in NPPES has a taxonomy authorizing behavior analysis services. Compare billed service hours against the employer's payroll and contractor timesheets for the same dates.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Credential-to-code match: on claim line x rendering NPI, compute exact-match status between the provider's registry-verified credential and the credential required for the billed ABA CPT; fires on any registry mismatch; action prepay edit. 2) Impossible day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of timed ABA units multiplied by their defined minutes; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours; action claim suspension. 3) Payroll coverage: on provider NPI x pay period, compute billed service hours divided by paid staff hours in payroll records; fires when the ratio exceeds one; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Louisiana; U.S. Department of Justice Criminal Division, Fraud Section
FraudEntity: Jamie P. McNamara (operator/owner of laboratories in Louisiana and Texas)
FraudTypeAll: kickback_Bribery For Referral; FakeEncounter; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud; Falsify certificate
SchemeSummary: McNamara ran labs in Louisiana and Texas that obtained cancer and cardiovascular genetic testing orders from telemarketing call centers, with orders signed by purported telemedicine doctors who never treated or consulted the beneficiaries; he paid kickbacks disguised via sham contracts, shifted billing among his labs to evade scrutiny, and concealed his ownership by listing family members as owners. The labs billed Medicare over $174 million in about 18 months and were reimbursed over $55 million; the government seized luxury vehicles and over $7 million in bank accounts.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, check whether the ordering NPI on each cancer or cardiovascular panel CPT has any prior treating encounter with the beneficiary in claims history. Compute the count of distinct beneficiary states and lab NPIs served per telemedicine ordering NPI per week. Compare a lab's billed panel volume to its CLIA certificate scope and staffing declared at enrolment. Track abrupt shifts of the same ordering NPIs' volume from one lab NPI to a sibling lab NPI after audit contact. Match CMS-855B owner names against family surnames, shared addresses and payee bank accounts across the affiliated labs.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Orderer-beneficiary relationship: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the last E/M claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no treating encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit on genomic CPTs. 2) Lab-hopping continuity: on ordering NPI x month, compute the count of distinct billing lab NPIs and the share of volume migrating after a prior audit or denial event; fires when migration exceeds the ordering NPI's trailing baseline; action payment suspension across linked labs. 3) Ownership graph: on payee bank account x 855B address, compute the count of distinct lab NPIs and undisclosed common owners; fires when any exact registry mismatch with disclosed ownership exists; action site visit and prior-authorisation requirement.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Louisiana
FraudEntity: Jamie P. McNamara (operator/owner of laboratories)
State_County: Louisiana - New Orleans (Eastern District of Louisiana); Texas
FraudTypeAll: kickback_Bribery For Referral; FakeEncounter; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud; Falsify certificate
SchemeSummary: McNamara ran labs in Louisiana and Texas that billed Medicare over $174 million (receiving over $55 million) for cancer and cardiovascular genetic testing ordered via aggressive telemarketing, with orders signed by telemedicine doctors who never treated or consulted the beneficiaries; he paid kickbacks disguised as sham contracts, shifted billing among labs to evade scrutiny, and concealed his ownership by listing family members as owners on Medicare documents. Restitution of over $55 million plus $7 million forfeiture was ordered.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, verify whether the ordering NPI on each genomic panel claim has any prior encounter claim with that beneficiary. Count distinct beneficiaries and states per telemedicine ordering NPI per week on lab orders. Compare paid dollars per beneficiary for cancer and cardiovascular panels against same-specialty lab peers. Compare CMS-855B disclosed owners against family-member names, shared addresses and payee accounts across affiliated lab NPIs. Detect the same ordering physicians' volume shifting between sibling lab NPIs after denials appear in remittance history.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the nearest treating E/M claim with the beneficiary; fires when none exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Telemarketed orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct billing lab NPIs on genomic CPT orders; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension. 3) Sibling-lab migration: on lab NPI cluster keyed by shared bank account, compute the ratio of billing volume transferred between NPIs within 90 days of a payer audit or denial spike; fires when the ratio exceeds the cluster's trailing baseline; action payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section; U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Louisiana
FraudEntity: Jamie P. McNamara (operator/owner of laboratories)
FraudTypeAll: kickback_Bribery For Referral; FakeEncounter; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud; Falsify certificate
SchemeSummary: McNamara operated laboratories in Louisiana and Texas that billed Medicare over $174 million (receiving over $55 million) for cancer and cardiovascular genetic testing, using doctors' orders obtained from telemarketers and call centers and signed by telemedicine doctors who never treated or consulted the beneficiaries; he paid kickbacks disguised as sham contracts, shifted billing among his labs to evade scrutiny, and hid his ownership by listing family members as owners on Medicare documents.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, confirm each genomic test claim has an ordering NPI with a documented prior treating relationship in the beneficiary's claims. Compute per-ordering-NPI weekly counts of distinct beneficiaries against feasible consultation minutes. Compare CMS-855B ownership disclosures against relatives' names, shared addresses and shared payee bank accounts among affiliated labs. Compute the share of a lab's beneficiaries with no oncology or cardiology diagnosis history supporting the panel billed. Compare marketer payments in submitted contracts against per-test volume to detect volume-based compensation.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Treating-relationship edit: on claim line, compute the gap in days between panel date of service and the nearest E/M claim linking ordering NPI and beneficiary; fires when no such claim exists; action prepay edit. 2) Ordering throughput: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiaries with signed genomic orders divided by billed consult minutes; fires when implied per-patient time is physically impossible within a 24-hour day; action claim suspension. 3) Hidden ownership match: on lab NPI, compute exact-match count between 855B owner fields and the payee bank account signatories or relatives listed on affiliated NPIs; fires on any registry mismatch; action site visit and payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
FraudEntity: Christopher Lee Carroll (co-owner, Square One Group LLC and Whiskey Dix Big Truck Repair LLC); George Reed (co-owner, Square One Group LLC); Whiskey Dix Big Truck Repair LLC (company)
FraudTypeAll: Covid or General Loan Fraud; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud
SchemeSummary: Carroll and Reed, owners of a timeshare exit company, submitted a false April 2020 PPP loan application for $1.2 million that listed their wives as owners to conceal Carroll's status as a paroled felon, then falsely certified in a forgiveness application that the funds went to payroll while Carroll instead used them to start a trucking company and cut employee health insurance; they later obtained a second PPP loan of over $1.6 million and took $660,000 in owner draws. Carroll was sentenced to 108 months and $3 million restitution and Reed to time served with the same $3 million restitution; unrelated Clean Air Act and witness-tampering counts were also part of Carroll's conviction.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim here and no adjudication point, so no payer edit could have stopped it. The nearest detection route is SBA loan-application screening comparing listed owners against felony-disclosure answers and state corporate registry officers. A second route is matching certified payroll headcount on the forgiveness application to IRS Form 941 and state unemployment wage filings. Bank monitoring of loan-account outflows to owner draws and a new unrelated trucking entity is the third route.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) Forgiveness payroll reconciliation: on borrower EIN, compute the difference between certified payroll spend and quarterly Form 941 wages plus state UI wage records; fires when certified spend exceeds reported wages; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of West Virginia
FraudEntity: David M. Anderson (physician)
SchemeSummary: A Morgantown physician filed false federal tax returns over a four-year period that understated his taxable income and included false claims to reduce his tax liability, causing an IRS loss of $143,599; he was sentenced to six months in prison plus three years of supervised release.
WaysToIdentify: This is an individual income tax matter with no claim submitted to any health payer and no adjudication point. The nearest detection route is IRS return matching of reported income against Forms 1099 and payer remittance totals paid to the practice TIN. A second route is comparing the practice's deposited receipts in bank records to gross receipts reported on Schedule C.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) Payer-to-return income match: on provider TIN x tax year, compute the gap between total remittances issued and income reported on the filed return; fires when the reported figure is below remittances issued; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
FraudEntity: CIE Tours International Inc. (tour company owned by the government of Ireland)
FraudTypeAll: Covid or General Loan Fraud; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud
SchemeSummary: CIE Tours International applied for and obtained two PPP loans totaling $3,410,300 and then obtained full forgiveness, despite being ineligible because it was owned by the government of Ireland and exceeded PPP employee size limits; resolved via False Claims Act qui tam settlement of $4,428,985.04, with the relator receiving $428,985.
WaysToIdentify: No health care claim exists, so no prepay adjudication control could apply to this loan forgiveness. The nearest detection route is SBA eligibility screening of the applicant's ownership field against foreign-government and affiliate ownership disclosures. A second route is affiliation-rule headcount testing using consolidated Form 941 employee counts across all commonly owned entities. Corporate registry and parent-company filings identify the sovereign owner at application, before disbursement.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) Sovereign and affiliate ownership screen: on borrower EIN, compute the count of disclosed owners matching foreign-government entities and the summed affiliate headcount from Form 941; fires when foreign-government ownership exists or headcount exceeds the program size standard; action prepay edit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Jersey
FraudEntity: Michael Kiszka; Gregory Kubina
State_County: New Jersey - Morris County (East Hanover); New Jersey - Ocean County (Whiting)
SchemeSummary: Two defendants allegedly obtained high-dosage oxycodone pills from several New Jersey doctors - Kiszka directly from certain doctors and by purchasing pills Kubina obtained from other doctors - and resold them to street-level drug users, diverting over 10,000 pills beginning around April 2024.
WaysToIdentify: At pharmacy adjudication, one beneficiary fills high-strength oxycodone NDCs from multiple prescriber NPIs within overlapping days-supply windows. The state PDMP shows the same patient dispensed by several pharmacies with no gap between fills. Claim history shows no imaging, procedure, or chronic pain diagnosis supporting the billed high morphine-milligram-equivalent NDCs. Prescription fills are consistently paid cash at some pharmacies and billed at others, visible in switch and PDMP records. FeaturesToCreate: 1) Prescriber shopping: on beneficiary x rolling 30 days, compute the distinct count of prescriber NPIs and pharmacy NPIs on Schedule II opioid NDC fills; fires when both counts exceed the calibrated percentile versus plan peers; action prepay edit. 2) MME overlap: on beneficiary x date, compute total morphine milligram equivalents from all overlapping days-supply opioid claims; fires when daily MME exceeds the plan's calibrated high-dose threshold; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Prescriber diversion profile: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the share of that NPI's dispensed prescriptions that are Schedule II opioids at maximum strength; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

SchemeSummary: Life Touch, a North Carolina substance abuse treatment company, and its owner/managers/compliance officer allegedly paid patients more than $1 million in gift cards based on the number of days per week they attended services, generating over $25 million in Medicaid payments, while staff also took kickbacks from a drug-testing lab and lied to Medicaid auditors (two defendants also charged with failure to file tax returns). Group session claims imply staff rendering NPI hours per date of service exceeding twenty-four hours. Ordering NPIs on brace and compression-device HCPCS have no prior E/M encounter with the beneficiary in claim history. The same beneficiary receives duplicate L-code braces from several supplier NPIs within a rolling month.

SchemeSummary: Garcia and a co-conspirator cashed more than 3,600 checks totaling about $28 million received by Tape Drywall Services from general contractors at a check cashing business, then distributed cash to foremen to pay construction workers off the books, failing to report wages or withhold and remit FICA and federal income taxes, causing over $4.2 million in loss to the IRS and also understating payroll to avoid workers' compensation insurance costs.

FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) Cash-out to wage reconciliation: on employer EIN x quarter, compute the ratio of checks cashed at money service businesses to wages reported on Form 941; fires when cashed receipts exceed reported wages by more than the industry-calibrated ratio; action postpay audit.

SchemeSummary: Nationwide 2025 takedown charging 324 defendants with over $14.6 billion in intended loss: Operation Gold Rush used foreign straw owners of dozens of medical supply companies and over one million stolen American identities to bill Medicare $10.6 billion for urinary catheters and other DME, laundering proceeds into cryptocurrency and foreign shell companies; other schemes included AI-generated fake beneficiary consent recordings feeding $703 million in nominee-owned DME/lab claims, $650 million in fraudulent Arizona Medicaid substance abuse treatment billing with kickbacks for homeless and Native American patient referrals, $1.1 billion in medically unnecessary amniotic wound allografts on hospice patients, 15 million diverted opioid pills, and $1.17 billion in telemedicine/genetic testing claims. WaysToIdentify: At enrolment, CMS-855S owner identities on dozens of supplier NPIs resolve to foreign addresses, shared phone numbers, or one mail-drop practice location. At adjudication, catheter HCPCS A4351 through A4353 quantities per beneficiary far exceed a month's medically plausible units. Beneficiaries on the claims have no prior urology, hospice, or wound-care encounter with any provider in claim history. Newly enrolled supplier NPIs jump from zero to peer-top-decile billing within weeks of a PECOS ownership change. Beneficiary identifiers appear on claims from many unrelated supplier NPIs spread across states never visited, per beneficiary residence ZIP.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Straw-owner graph: on CMS-855 enrolment record, compute the count of other enrolled NPIs sharing an owner SSN, bank account, address, or phone from PECOS; fires when that degree exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty enrollees; action site visit before billing privileges activate. 2) Catheter unit ceiling: on beneficiary x HCPCS x month, compute summed units and the distinct count of billing supplier NPIs; fires when units exceed the coverage-policy monthly maximum or supplier count exceeds one; action prepay edit. 3) New-supplier ramp: on supplier NPI x week, compute billed allowed amount divided by the provider's trailing twelve-week baseline since enrolment; fires when the ratio is above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension.

SchemeSummary: Four EDLA defendants charged as part of the 2025 national takedown: Roberts and Lee, co-owners of Luminus Diagnostics in Tifton, GA, allegedly paid/received kickbacks for genetic testing orders (including via purported telemedicine), used 'dummy proof' order forms with prepopulated diagnosis codes, and routed tests through another lab under a sham contract, causing over $30 million (Roberts) and about $24 million (Lee) in false Medicare claims with roughly $4.4 million and $4 million paid; Peyroux allegedly paid kickbacks for Medicare beneficiary identifiers and fabricated recordings of purported beneficiaries to bill about $12.1 million (about $11 million paid) for unrequested over-the-counter COVID-19 tests, using sham agreements and false audit responses to conceal it; Francis allegedly embezzled HHS-grant and other federal funds from a New Orleans non-profit for personal events and Amazon purchases. SchemeSummary: Sales director for a mobile diagnostics company allegedly paid doctors cash and checks per transcranial doppler (TCD) ultrasound they ordered, disguised through sham rental and administrative services agreements purporting to be fair-market-value payments, generating roughly $70.6 million in Medicare billing for medically unnecessary brain scans.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, transcranial doppler CPT volume per ordering NPI rises in near-linear step with payments recorded to that NPI in vendor ledgers. Ordering physicians bill TCD studies for beneficiaries with no stroke, syncope, or cerebrovascular diagnosis on any claim. The mobile diagnostic entity's place-of-service code shows office testing at practices with no imaging equipment on their CMS-855 enrolment. A small set of ordering NPIs accounts for nearly all of the billing entity's TCD claims. Sham space and administrative agreements name physician landlords whose leased square footage does not appear in the practice's enrolment address record.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Orderer concentration: on billing entity NPI x quarter, compute the share of TCD CPT claim lines contributed by the top five ordering NPIs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty imaging peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Indication mismatch: on ordering NPI x CPT, compute the share of TCD studies with no cerebrovascular ICD-10 code in the beneficiary's twelve-month claim history; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action prepay edit. 3) Per-test payment correlation: on ordering NPI x month, compute the correlation between ordered TCD counts and disclosed rental or administrative payments from the entity's financial-relationship disclosures; fires when ordered volume scales with payments; action postpay audit.

SchemeSummary: Nearly 50 defendants charged across 22 SDTX cases in the 2025 national takedown, with over $360 million billed to Medicare/Medicaid and roughly 12 million controlled-substance pills diverted: Ogudo/Martinez enrolled non-terminally-ill elderly beneficiaries in United Palliative & Hospice while paying kickbacks to group-home owners, a psychiatric hospital discharge coordinator, and physician Munoz to certify terminal illness ($110 million); Jenson and Romero billed over $90 million for skin-substitute products for patients with no qualifying wounds and falsified records to show chronic, improving wounds; Harper billed $115 million for kickback-induced, medically unnecessary genetic/diagnostic lab tests through shell companies and a fraudulent equipment loan; Mitchell collected $9.9 million from the COVID-19 Uninsured Program for in-office consultations never provided; Johnson billed Medicaid $793,804 (receiving $331,112) for mental health therapy never provided; and pill-mill/pharmacy rings (Peterson, Qayum, Bowers, Stokes, Sampson, Betts et al.) sold opioid prescriptions for cash and diverted millions of doses to the black market. Skin-substitute HCPCS Q-codes are billed with no prior wound-care encounter or wound measurement documented in prior-authorisation records. Genetic testing CPT lines route through shell laboratory NPIs whose enrolment addresses match the ordering entity's address in PECOS. COVID Uninsured Program consultation claims name patients with concurrent active insurance coverage in eligibility files.

SchemeSummary: A Las Vegas nurse practitioner applied medically unnecessary amniotic wound allografts to Medicare beneficiaries obtained through illegal kickbacks and bribes, and her wound care company billed Medicare approximately $14.3 million, of which Medicare paid about $9.1 million.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, amniotic allograft Q-code claim lines bill square centimetres far exceeding the wound area recorded in prior-authorisation documentation. The rendering nurse practitioner NPI's allograft spend per beneficiary sits far above same-specialty wound-care peers. SchemeSummary: Khan, through his NEMCA network of New England clinics, required patients to pay $250 in cash for high-dose buprenorphine prescriptions, falsified medical records to justify the prescribing, and lowered dosages for patients who could not pay in full; he diverted the cash proceeds for personal use including an airplane and properties, and was ordered to forfeit $75,000 plus a $20,000 fine.
WaysToIdentify: In PDMP data, one prescriber NPI's buprenorphine prescriptions cluster at maximum daily doses far above same-specialty peers. Dispensing records show most of this prescriber's patients paying cash while holding active insurance coverage in eligibility files. Prescribed dosage changes per patient correlate with payment status rather than any documented clinical assessment in records requested by ADR. Patient counts per prescriber NPI exceed the DATA-waiver or practice-capacity limits recorded with DEA registration. Visit intervals in PDMP show refills issued on dates with no corresponding E/M claim for that beneficiary.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) High-dose buprenorphine share: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the share of buprenorphine prescriptions at or above the maximum recommended daily dose; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Cash-pay divergence: on prescriber NPI x month, compute the share of dispensed prescriptions paid cash by patients with active coverage in eligibility files; fires when above the provider's trailing baseline and peer percentile; action postpay audit. 3) Refill without encounter: on beneficiary x prescription fill date, compute days since the nearest E/M claim from that prescriber; fires when no encounter exists within the plan's required visit interval; action prepay edit.
