A second route is comparing supplier purchase and delivery records for sump pump units against the number of homes invoiced.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on invoice line x property address, compute the count of matching independent inspection sign-offs and material receipts for the certified component and withhold payment when the count is zero.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section; U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Maryland
FraudEntity: Patrick Britton-Harr (owner of Provista Health and AeroVanti Inc.); Provista Health; AeroVanti Inc.
FraudTypeAll: Phantom Claims; FakeEncounter; Falsify certificate; Wire Fraud; Covid or General Loan Fraud
SchemeSummary: Britton-Harr allegedly used his company Provista Health to offer COVID-19 screening tests to nursing home patients nationwide and then billed Medicare for expensive respiratory pathogen panel (RPP) tests that were medically unnecessary, never ordered by a treating physician, and in many cases never performed, including for deceased patients - more than $15 million billed and over $5 million paid. A second indictment charges wire fraud for misappropriating nearly $15 million in upfront payments from about 100 'Top Gun' members of his AeroVanti private jet club, plus obtaining a $1.5 million loan by withholding material information.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compare respiratory pathogen panel dates of service to the Death Master File date of death for each beneficiary. Check whether an ordering NPI on the panel claim has any treating relationship with the nursing home resident in prior claims. Compute the ratio of RPP CPT 87633 claims to COVID-only 87635 claims per laboratory NPI versus peer labs. Count distinct facility ZIPs and states served by one lab NPI in a week against its CMS-855B enrolment service area. Compare specimen collection dates on claims against facility visitor and staffing logs obtained during a site visit.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Deceased-beneficiary testing: on claim line, compute days between the specimen date of service and the Death Master File date of death; fires when service date is after death; action prepay edit. 2) Reflex panel ratio: on laboratory NPI x month, compute RPP CPT units divided by COVID-only test units; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty laboratory peers; action payment suspension. 3) Orderer relationship: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute the count of prior encounters between the ordering NPI and the beneficiary; fires when zero for a facility-wide batch of same-day specimens; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Maryland
FraudEntity: Patrick Britton-Harr (owner of Provista Health and AeroVanti, Inc.)
FraudTypeAll: Phantom Claims; FakeEncounter; Wire Fraud; Falsify certificate
SchemeSummary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, defendant offered COVID-19 screening to nursing home patients nationwide and, through his company Provista Health, billed Medicare over $15 million for expensive respiratory pathogen panel tests that were medically unnecessary, not ordered by treating physicians, and in many cases never performed - including for deceased patients; Medicare paid over $5 million. A second indictment charges wire fraud for misappropriating roughly $15 million in upfront payments from nearly 100 'Top Gun' members of his private jet club AeroVanti.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, match respiratory pathogen panel service dates against the Death Master File date of death. Verify the ordering NPI has a prior treating encounter with the nursing home resident in the beneficiary's claim history. Compute the share of a lab's volume in high-reimbursement panel codes versus single-target COVID codes relative to peer labs. Count distinct facilities and states billed by one lab NPI per week against its CMS-855B enrolled service area. Compare billed specimen counts against courier and reagent purchase records collected on a site visit.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Post-death service date: on claim line, compute the gap in days between date of service and Death Master File date of death; fires when positive; action prepay edit. 2) Panel-versus-single ratio: on laboratory NPI x month, compute panel CPT units divided by total respiratory test units; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Batch orderer anomaly: on ordering NPI x date of service, compute distinct beneficiaries with same-day panel orders; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers with no prior encounter on file; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida
FraudEntity: Vascular and Interventional Specialists, LLC (VIS) (endovascular surgery center); Vascular and Spine Institute, Inc. (VSI) (billing entity); Oscar Sosa, M.D. (practitioner); Osmany DeAngelo, D.O. (practitioner)
SchemeSummary: Providers performed hundreds of percutaneous transluminal angioplasties without any diagnostic inquiry or clinical diagnosis supporting medical necessity, then billed Medicare and other federal health programs for the medically unnecessary procedures; resolved for $810,301 following a qui tam suit whose relator receives about $186,369.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, check for a preceding diagnostic angiogram or non-invasive vascular study claim before each angioplasty CPT on the beneficiary. Compute angioplasties per rendering NPI per year against same-specialty peers in the payer's remittance history. Check the beneficiary's diagnosis history for peripheral arterial disease or critical limb ischemia codes supporting intervention. Compute the rate of repeat angioplasties on the same vessel territory per beneficiary within short intervals. Compare procedures per operator per day against realistic procedure room minutes recorded on the facility claim.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Missing diagnostic workup: on claim line x beneficiary, compute the count of qualifying non-invasive vascular study or diagnostic angiography claims in the lookback before the angioplasty date; fires when zero; action prepay edit. 2) Operator volume outlier: on rendering NPI x year, compute angioplasty CPT counts divided by distinct beneficiaries; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit. 3) Repeat intervention rate: on beneficiary x rendering NPI, compute the count of angioplasties on the same limb within a rolling year; fires when above the provider's own trailing baseline and peer rate; action documentation request (ADR).
FeatureCategory: Coverage, Indication and Prior Auth Edits

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of California
FraudEntity: Jessa Zayas (CEO and owner of Healing Hands Hospice and Humane Love Hospice); Healing Hands Hospice; Humane Love Hospice
State_County: California - Fresno County; California - Kern County; California - Los Angeles County (Van Nuys)
FraudTypeAll: Falsify certificate; IdentityFraud; Phantom Claims; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud
SchemeSummary: Zayas, owner of two Van Nuys hospice companies, recruited over 100 residents of Fresno and Kern County retirement homes during after-hours door-knocking visits to obtain their Medicare information, then billed Medicare for hospice care with false representations that the patients were terminally ill and submitted forged physician certifications when Medicare requested supporting documentation; payments went to bank accounts she controlled.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, check the beneficiary's prior claims for any terminal diagnosis or declining-status utilization before the hospice election date. Compare the certifying physician NPI on the CMS hospice certification against that physician's own claim history with the beneficiary. Compute the share of the hospice's patients with live discharges or stays exceeding the six-month benchmark. Count distinct beneficiaries recruited from the same retirement home address across the hospice's admissions file. Verify the certifying physician's signature on documentation returned to an ADR against the state board licence file and PECOS.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Certifier-relationship gap: on hospice election x certifying physician NPI, compute the count of prior encounters between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when zero; action prepay edit. 2) Long-stay live-discharge rate: on hospice NPI x quarter, compute the share of beneficiaries with stays beyond 180 days or discharged alive; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-state hospice peers; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension. 3) Address clustering: on hospice NPI x residential address, compute distinct beneficiaries admitted within a rolling 90 days; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action site visit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Colorado
FraudEntity: Mt. San Rafael Hospital and Rural Health Clinic; Dr. Sheryll Castro-Flores (physician); Dr. Joseph Jimenez (physician); Dr. Douglas McFarland (physician)
PayerName: Medicare; other federal health care programs
SchemeSummary: Three hospital-employed physicians allegedly issued invalid controlled-substance prescriptions, including high-dose opioids and dangerous combinations, without legitimate medical purpose and despite red flags (early refills, cash payments despite insurance, long-distance patients), and the hospital caused claims for those invalid prescriptions to be billed to Medicare and other federal health programs. Combined $650,000 payment across the hospital ($325,000) and the three doctors ($112,500, $112,500, $100,000).
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compute daily morphine milligram equivalents per beneficiary from NDC, strength and days supply on pharmacy claims. Detect overlapping opioid and benzodiazepine fills from the same prescriber NPI in the beneficiary's pharmacy claim history. Compute the gap in days between successive fills of the same NDC to identify early refills against days supply. Compare the distance between beneficiary residence ZIP and prescriber practice ZIP in NPPES for long-distance patient patterns. Compare cash-paid fills reported in the state PDMP against the beneficiary's active insurance coverage.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) High-MME prescriber: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the share of patients whose daily MME from NDC strength and days supply exceeds the CDC threshold; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Dangerous combination: on beneficiary x prescriber NPI, compute overlapping days supply of opioid and benzodiazepine or carisoprodol NDCs; fires when overlap days are above zero repeatedly; action prepay edit. 3) Early refill gap: on beneficiary x NDC, compute days between fill date and prior fill date minus prior days supply; fires when negative; action claim suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Michigan
FraudEntity: Charise Valentine (doctor); Michele Ritter (doctor, co-defendant); Iris Winchester (clinic operator); Joyce Robinson (patient recruiter); Orthopedic Medical Building (sham clinic)
State_County: Michigan - Oakland County (Southfield); Michigan - Oakland County (Oak Park)
FraudTypeAll: Drug_Prescriptions; kickback_Bribery For Referral; Falsify certificate; FakeEncounter
SchemeSummary: At a cash-only sham clinic operating from an Oak Park warehouse, Dr. Valentine issued over 3,000 medically unnecessary opioid prescriptions (more than 200,000 Oxycodone/Oxymorphone pills worth over $5.2 million) to 'patients' brought in by recruiters, who paid $200-500 per prescription based on drug quantity and dosage, plus cash for fabricated medical records; Valentine received about 50% of proceeds (over $500,000 cash) and was paid only when she wrote a prescription. Co-defendants including the clinic operator, another doctor, and a recruiter previously pleaded guilty and were sentenced.
WaysToIdentify: In the state PDMP, compute oxycodone and oxymorphone pill counts dispensed per prescriber NPI per month against same-specialty peers. Compute the share of that prescriber's prescriptions paid in cash despite the patient holding active coverage. Compute the distance from prescriber practice address in NPPES to patient residence ZIPs on dispensed prescriptions. Check whether the prescriber submits any E/M claims corresponding to the visits that supposedly generated the prescriptions. Compare the prescribing address to the CMS-855I practice location, since a warehouse site indicates no clinical facility.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Opioid volume outlier: on prescriber NPI x month, compute total oxycodone and oxymorphone dosage units dispensed from PDMP NDC and quantity fields; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Prescriptions without encounters: on prescriber NPI x month, compute dispensed controlled prescriptions divided by billed E/M encounters; fires when the ratio far exceeds one against peer baseline; action payment suspension. 3) Patient travel radius: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the median miles between practice ZIP and patient ZIP on controlled fills; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action site visit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Central District of California
FraudEntity: Tonmoy Sharma (founder and former CEO, Sovereign Health Group); Paul Jin Sen Khor (cash management and accounts payable supervisor); Sovereign Health Group; Vedanta Laboratories Inc.
State_County: California - Orange County (San Clemente, Tustin, Irvine)
PayerName: Private health insurers (out-of-network commercial plans, including ACA-subsidized private plans)
FraudTypeAll: Wire Fraud; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud; kickback_Bribery For Referral; IdentityFraud; Phantom Claims; Falsify certificate; Upcoding
SchemeSummary: Sovereign Health Group allegedly submitted over $149 million in fraudulent claims to private insurers for addiction/mental health treatment billed at high out-of-network rates, using a sham 'foundation' to harvest patients' identities and then falsifying insurance applications (fake qualifying life events, misstated income) to surreptitiously enroll patients in ACA-subsidized private plans instead of lower-paying Medicaid. It also billed more than $29 million for comprehensive urinalysis panel tests (through its Vedanta Laboratories) that ordering physicians never authorized or that were billed after physicians left, and paid over $21 million in kickbacks to patient brokers disguised as 'marketing hours' under sham contracts.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compute definitive urine drug testing units per patient per week against clinical guideline frequency for the treatment level billed. Verify the ordering NPI on urinalysis claims was actively affiliated with the facility on the date of service using NPPES and payroll rosters. Match new-enrollee applications against reported qualifying life events and income, since clustered enrollments from one facility address signal broker activity. Compare patient residence states to the facility state to identify brokered out-of-state admissions in the eligibility file. Compute marketing payments per admitted patient recorded in the facility's contractor invoices against admissions volume.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Urinalysis frequency: on beneficiary x facility TIN x week, compute definitive drug test panel units billed; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-modality treatment peers; action prepay edit. 2) Ordering-provider validity: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute whether the date of service falls inside that provider's active affiliation and licence dates in NPPES and the state board file; fires on exact registry mismatch; action claim suspension. 3) Enrollment clustering: on facility address x plan enrollment month, compute distinct new marketplace enrollees sharing that mailing address or contact phone; fires when above one household equivalent; action payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Washington
FraudEntity: William Philip Werschler (dermatologist, owner); Spokane Dermatology Clinic; Premier Clinical Research L.L.C.; 3rd and Sherman Plaza L.L.C.
SchemeSummary: Dermatologist applied for COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans for his dermatology clinic and related businesses, then spent the proceeds on prohibited personal purposes - $252,375 on two Porsche automobiles and $553,143 to purchase two properties across from his clinic - resolving False Claims Act claims and related criminal charges for $1.4 million.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point in this disaster loan case. The nearest detection route is matching EIDL disbursement bank accounts to subsequent vehicle title and real property deed records in the borrower's name. A second route is comparing certified working-capital use on the loan application against the borrower's business bank statements before further draws.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on borrower bank account, compute the share of loan proceeds transferred within 90 days to titled vehicle purchases or real estate escrow and refer when that share is above zero for prohibited categories.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Washington
FraudEntity: Dr. Duncan Lahtinen (licensed physician)
SchemeSummary: Dr. Lahtinen issued over 1,400 controlled substance prescriptions to thirteen identified patients between 2017 and 2025 - often dangerous combinations of opioids, benzodiazepines, sedatives, and carisoprodol - ignoring red flags of substance abuse, making him liable for civil penalties under the Controlled Substances Act and False Claims Act; he paid $120,000 in penalties.
WaysToIdentify: In the state PDMP, compute overlapping days supply of opioid, benzodiazepine, sedative and carisoprodol NDCs per patient for one prescriber. Compute daily morphine milligram equivalents from NDC strength, quantity and days supply on each patient's dispensing history. Compute the count of distinct controlled substance schedules prescribed to the same patient in a rolling month. Compare the prescriber's controlled prescription count per patient against same-specialty peers in the dispensing file. Check for early refills using the gap between fill date and the prior fill's exhaustion date.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Quadruple-therapy overlap: on beneficiary x prescriber NPI, compute overlapping days supply across opioid, benzodiazepine, sedative and carisoprodol NDC classes; fires when three or more overlap on the same day; action prepay edit. 2) MME concentration: on prescriber NPI x quarter, compute the share of patients above the CDC daily MME threshold; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Early refill gap: on beneficiary x NDC, compute fill date minus prior fill date minus prior days supply; fires when negative repeatedly for the same prescriber; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Louisiana
FraudEntity: Ashley Hymel (executive assistant at Company 1)
SchemeSummary: Hymel, an executive assistant, allegedly used her employer's company credit card to embezzle at least $130,663.92 from the company, charged by bill of information as wire fraud.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point in this employee card embezzlement. The nearest detection route is reconciling corporate card transaction files against approved vendor lists and expense receipts each month. A second route is comparing per-cardholder monthly spend to that cardholder's own trailing baseline in the card issuer statement file.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on cardholder account x month, compute the sum of transactions lacking a matched receipt or approved vendor code and escalate when that sum exceeds the cardholder's trailing baseline.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Louisiana
FraudEntity: Ashley Hymel (executive assistant at Company 1)
SchemeSummary: Hymel, an executive assistant, used her employer's company credit card to embezzle at least $130,663.92 from the employer (Company 1); she pled guilty to wire fraud and agreed to repay the full amount.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point in this corporate card embezzlement. The nearest detection route is monthly reconciliation of card transaction files to receipts and merchant category codes by someone other than the cardholder. A second route is trending each cardholder's spend against their own prior-year baseline in the issuer statement file.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on cardholder account x month, compute unreceipted spend and personal merchant category spend as a share of total charges and escalate when above the cardholder's trailing baseline.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Florida
FraudEntity: Daniel Tharp (managing director, Hangar X Holdings, LLC); Hangar X Holdings, LLC
SchemeSummary: As managing director of Hangar X Holdings, LLC, Tharp was responsible for collecting and paying over the company's trust fund taxes (income, Medicare, and Social Security taxes) withheld from employee wages; from October 2014 through December 2019 the company withheld these taxes but Tharp knowingly failed to remit over $1.2 million to the IRS.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim and no payer adjudication point in this trust fund tax case. The nearest detection route is comparing wages and withholding reported on Forms W-2 and W-3 against Form 941 deposits actually received by the IRS. A second route is flagging employers filing 941s while making no corresponding EFTPS deposits over consecutive quarters.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. Nearest control outside the claims system: on employer EIN x quarter, compute withheld tax reported on Form 941 minus deposits received through EFTPS and open a trust fund recovery inquiry when the difference is positive across consecutive quarters.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
FraudEntity: Dr. Sonny Saggar (doctor, operator of St. Louis General Hospital urgent care locations); Renita Barringer (office manager)
State_County: Missouri - St. Louis (downtown St. Louis and Creve Coeur)
FraudTypeAll: Falsify certificate; FakeEncounter; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud; kickback_Bribery For Referral
SchemeSummary: Saggar and his office manager hired assistant physicians (medical school graduates without residency) to see patients at two urgent care/primary care locations but billed Medicare and Missouri Medicaid as if Saggar personally performed the services, even when he was out of town; he paid physicians stipends up to $480/month to sign collaborative practice arrangement forms filed with the state medical board to falsely show supervision, used APs at a non-underserved location, and concealed from Medicaid that a co-conspirator physician with suspended billing privileges was providing services. Loss of $742,528 attributed jointly to Saggar and Barringer (who awaits sentencing).
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compare the rendering NPI on E/M claims against travel or absence evidence such as out-of-state card and claim activity on the same dates. Count services billed under one supervising NPI per day and divide by a physically possible workday of 24 hours. Check the state medical board collaborative practice arrangement file for assistant physician names not matching any rendering NPI on submitted claims. Match the practice service location on the CMS-855B against the HRSA medically underserved area file required for assistant physician supervision. Screen every individual furnishing services at the TIN against OIG LEIE and state Medicaid suspended-provider lists at credentialing.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Solo-rendering impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total billed E/M time-equivalent minutes across all service locations; fires when the sum exceeds 24 hours or overlapping minutes occur at two locations; action prepay edit. 2) Supervision registry mismatch: on rendering NPI x practice TIN, compute an exact match rate between billed rendering NPIs and the state board collaborative practice arrangement roster plus the HRSA underserved-site list; fires on any exact registry mismatch; action claim suspension and site visit. 3) Excluded furnisher linkage: on practice TIN, compute the count of payroll or credentialed clinicians appearing on OIG LEIE or state suspension files; fires when the count exceeds zero; action payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
FraudEntity: Dr. Asim Muhammad Ali (physician, owner of Central Diagnostic Laboratory and Institute for Pain Management LLC); Dr. Mohd Azfar Malik (owner of Psych Care Consultants LLC)
PayerName: Medicare; Missouri Medicaid; TRICARE; private health insurers
FraudTypeAll: kickback_Bribery For Referral; Drug_Prescriptions; Phantom Claims; Falsify certificate
SchemeSummary: Dr. Ali paid kickbacks for urine specimens referred to his own lab, Central Diagnostic Laboratory, and pre-signed/issued controlled-substance prescriptions for pain-management patients he never examined; in a separate case he performed services for Psych Care Consultants' Medicare patients but billed under Dr. Malik's name and Medicare number for 'annual wellness visits' conducted only by phone. Dr. Malik separately billed Medicare, Medicaid and private insurers for in-person services while out of the state or country and for ketamine infusions performed by Ali, who lacked DEA registration. Figures span both defendants: Ali ordered to pay $1,845,916 plus $3,902 restitution; Malik fined $20,000 and ordered to pay $19,442 restitution with five years probation.}
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compute the share of urine drug testing claims whose ordering NPI has a PECOS or CMS-855 ownership link to the billing laboratory. Compare annual wellness visit claims billed as in-person place of service 11 against telecom-only documentation and absent telehealth modifiers. Match rendering NPI dates of service against border-crossing or out-of-country evidence and same-day claims in another jurisdiction. Verify the prescriber on controlled-substance claims holds an active DEA registration at the NDC dispensing date in the DEA registrant file. Count patients with controlled-substance prescriptions but no prior in-person E/M encounter with the prescribing NPI in the payer's own claim history.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Self-referral share: on ordering NPI x laboratory TIN, compute the proportion of the lab's toxicology claims traceable to orderers with PECOS ownership or compensation links; fires when the proportion exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit and postpay audit. 2) DEA registry mismatch: on claim line, compute an exact match of prescriber NPI to an active DEA registration covering the billed NDC schedule on the fill date; fires on any mismatch or expired registration; action prepay edit. 3) Absent-clinician billing: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the count of face-to-face place-of-service 11 services on days with documented absence or with claims filed in a distant state; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York
FraudEntity: Omnicare (long-term care pharmacy); CVS Health Corporation (parent company)
SchemeSummary: A civil False Claims Act jury found that Omnicare, the nation's largest long-term care pharmacy, dispensed drugs to elderly and disabled residents of assisted living and other residential long-term care facilities without valid prescriptions, submitting over three million false claims to Medicare, Medicaid and TRICARE; damages were assessed at $135,592,814, trebled to $406,778,442, and parent CVS Health was found liable for causing the false claims.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, check each long-term care pharmacy claim for a prescriber NPI, written date, and prescription number linked to a valid original or refill authorization. Compute the days between the fill date and the last valid prescription expiration or last authorized refill on the pharmacy's own dispensing records. Compare the residence facility type on the beneficiary's claim to the drug's authorization source, since assisted living residents lack a chart-order equivalent. Count dispensings continuing after the prescriber NPI shows no encounter with that beneficiary for the diagnosis in the payer's claim history. Sample cycle-fill records against the pharmacy's electronic prescription files at audit rather than accepting attestation.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Refill authorization expiry: on beneficiary x NDC x pharmacy NPI, compute days between fill date and the expiration of the last documented prescription authorization; fires when the gap is positive with no new authorization on file; action prepay edit. 2) Order-source mismatch: on claim line, compute an exact match between the residence facility type and the presence of a prescriber-signed prescription record rather than a facility chart order; fires on mismatch for assisted living or residential settings; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Prescriber-contact gap: on beneficiary x prescriber NPI, compute months since the last paid encounter with that prescriber while chronic fills continue; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-setting peers; action postpay audit.
FeatureCategory: Coverage, Indication and Prior Auth Edits

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois
FraudEntity: Shawn Bashir (creator of Success for Kids and Growing Kids Therapy)
State_County: Illinois - Lake County (Grayslake); Illinois - Cook County (Chicago)
SchemeSummary: Bashir allegedly created fictitious entities, Success for Kids and Growing Kids Therapy, purporting to provide early intervention therapy services to children, and submitted about $17.3 million in claims to a private insurer for therapy never provided, causing at least $1.4 million in payments; also charged with two counts of aggravated identity theft.
WaysToIdentify: At enrolment, verify the entity's legal name, TIN, and address in NPPES against state licensure and secretary-of-state incorporation records for early intervention providers. At adjudication, count therapy claims whose rendering clinician NPI has no active state licence in the licensing board file. Compare claimed session dates for each child against the beneficiary's other claims showing school, hospital, or travel conflicts. Compute the ratio of billed charges to any prior remittance history for a newly enrolled entity with no ramp period. Check whether multiple provider entities submit for the same children from one bank account or shared address in the payer's payment file.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) New-entity billing ramp: on billing NPI x month, compute total billed charges divided by the provider's trailing baseline since enrolment; fires when a first-year entity exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit and site visit. 2) Unlicensed renderer: on claim line, compute an exact match between rendering NPI and an active state therapy licence covering the date of service; fires on any registry mismatch; action claim suspension. 3) Shared-payment cluster: on bank account, compute the count of distinct billing NPIs and distinct entity names receiving remittances; fires when the count exceeds one without disclosed common ownership on enrolment forms; action payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois
FraudEntity: Advanced Inventory Management, Inc. (medical device company); Anthony Iaderosa (sole owner and CEO)
FraudTypeAll: Device, DME; Other - FDA Submission Fraud
SchemeSummary: The company imported medical products from international distributors at lower prices, used a hair dryer to remove labels restricting resale to specified foreign countries, and resold the misbranded devices in the U.S. at 35-50% markups, earning about $500,000 in profits while concealing the practice from the FDA and causing false statements to customs agents; resolved via deferred prosecution agreements with a $1 million fine.
WaysToIdentify: There is no payer claim and no adjudication point here, since the harm is importation and resale of misbranded devices rather than billing. The nearest detection route is customs entry data and FDA import records compared against the distributor's domestic sales invoices and device labeling. A payer-side proxy exists only if such devices later appear on DMEPOS claims with serial or lot numbers absent from the manufacturer's U.S. distribution pedigree.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) Pedigree mismatch: on supplier NPI x HCPCS, compute the count of dispensed device serial or lot numbers absent from the manufacturer's authorized U.S. distribution file; fires when the count exceeds zero; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Illinois
FraudEntity: Mona Ghosh (physician, owner of Progressive Women's Healthcare, S.C.); Progressive Women's Healthcare, S.C.
FraudTypeAll: FakeEncounter; Phantom Claims; Upcoding; Falsify certificate
SchemeSummary: OB/GYN owner billed Medicaid, TRICARE and private insurers for nonexistent and medically unnecessary procedures (endometrial ablations and biopsies, ultrasounds, vaccinations, blood and STD tests), some performed without patient consent, and inflated the length/complexity of in-office and telemedicine visits using higher-paying codes, supporting the claims with falsified patient medical records.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compute the share of the practice's E/M claims billed at the two highest levels against same-specialty peer distributions. Count endometrial ablation and biopsy CPT claims per 100 female beneficiaries relative to obstetrics-gynecology peers in the same state. Compare telehealth-modifier visits billed at high complexity levels with the total minutes claimed by that rendering NPI per day. Check for repeat ablation claims on the same beneficiary, since the procedure is not normally repeated at short intervals. Cross-check STD and blood panel orders against any documented diagnosis code supporting screening in the beneficiary's other claims.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) High-level E/M concentration: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of level 4 and 5 E/M lines to all E/M lines for both in-person and telehealth places of service; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit and documentation request (ADR). 2) Procedure saturation: on rendering NPI, compute ablation and biopsy CPT counts per 100 attributed female beneficiaries; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Repeat-ablation impossibility: on beneficiary x CPT, compute the gap in days between successive endometrial ablation claims; fires when a second claim occurs within the clinically implausible window; action claim suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Pennsylvania
FraudEntity: Kelley Oliver-Hollis (owner of SerenityCare LLC); SerenityCare LLC
FraudTypeAll: Upcoding; Falsify certificate; Wire Fraud; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud
SchemeSummary: Owner of SerenityCare LLC, a Penn Hills facility serving residents with intellectual disabilities, allegedly overbilled Pennsylvania Medicaid for services provided from December 2016 to July 2023, and made false statements and concealed material facts relating to health care matters; superseding indictment adds money laundering and misuse of Social Security benefits as a representative payee.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compare billed personal care units per resident per day against the authorized units on the state prior-authorization and person-centered service plan record. Compute total direct-care staff hours from payroll and EVV records versus billed units for the same week. Check the billed procedure and modifier against the resident's assessed level of need in the state assessment file to detect a higher-paying tier. Match dates of service against hospital or emergency inpatient claims in the resident's other claims showing absence from the facility. Verify representative payee status and Social Security benefit flows against the provider's room-and-board charges at enrolment.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Authorization overage: on beneficiary x provider NPI x week, compute billed units minus prior-authorized units from the state service plan; fires when the difference is positive; action prepay edit. 2) Staffing capacity: on provider NPI x week, compute billed service hours divided by payroll and EVV-documented direct-care hours; fires when the ratio exceeds one; action payment suspension and site visit. 3) Tier upcoding: on beneficiary x claim line, compute an exact match between the billed level-of-need modifier and the tier in the state assessment record; fires on mismatch; action claim suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Florida
FraudEntity: Mihir Taneja; Larry Smith (owner of Z Stat Medical, LLC d/b/a Oldsmar Pharmacy); Z Stat Medical, LLC d/b/a Oldsmar Pharmacy; Centurion Compounding, Inc. (marketing company)
State_County: Florida - Hillsborough County (Tampa); Florida - Pinellas County (Oldsmar)
SchemeSummary: Taneja and pharmacy owner Larry Smith negotiated an arrangement paying marketing company Centurion Compounding a percentage of profits from TRICARE claims it referred to Oldsmar Pharmacy, resulting in thousands of TRICARE claims for compounded pain and scar creams tainted by kickbacks from November 2014 to February 2015. Taneja agreed to pay $2 million, Smith previously paid $600,000, and Oldsmar Pharmacy returned over $19 million to TRICARE.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compute the share of a pharmacy's compound cream claims traceable to a single marketing entity's referring prescriber cluster. Compare average paid amount per compound NDC combination against the same drug class across peer pharmacies. Check whether prescriber NPIs on the compound claims are geographically distant from the pharmacy and from beneficiary residence ZIPs. Review the pharmacy's disclosed contracts and ownership on enrolment forms for percentage-of-revenue marketing arrangements. Count beneficiaries receiving high-cost scar and pain creams with no prior related diagnosis in their other claims.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Marketer funnel concentration: on pharmacy NPI x month, compute the share of compound claims from the top prescriber cluster and the distinct-referrer graph degree; fires when concentration exceeds the calibrated percentile versus peer pharmacies; action prepay edit. 2) Compound price outlier: on claim line, compute the paid amount per compound prescription against the same-ingredient distribution across peer pharmacies; fires when above the calibrated percentile; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Distance implausibility: on pharmacy NPI x prescriber NPI, compute the mean miles between prescriber practice address in NPPES and beneficiary residence ZIP; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peers; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
FraudEntity: Henry Ezeonyido (organizer); Brendon Ashe; Aqiyla Atherton (intermediary/recruiter); Darline Cobbler; Ariel Lambert
PayerName: Five unnamed private health insurance companies
SchemeSummary: Ezeonyido submitted over $1 million in false out-of-network reimbursement claims to five private health insurers for expensive medical treatment allegedly received and paid out-of-pocket while traveling abroad (including fake stabbings, gunshot wounds and hit-and-run injuries), supported by fabricated medical records, bank records and foreign police reports, although the purported patients were actually in the U.S.; insurers paid about $655,313, and beneficiaries kicked back a share to Ezeonyido, who kept roughly $396,998. Restitution ($655,313) and forfeiture ($396,998) figures are Ezeonyido's; his four co-defendants received probation.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, verify the foreign treating facility's name and address against recognized international provider directories before paying out-of-network reimbursement. Compare claimed treatment dates abroad with the member's domestic claims, pharmacy fills, and card activity in the same window. Count distinct member reimbursement requests sharing one mailing address, bank account, or submitter email in the payer's payment file. Check submitted invoices and police reports for identical templates, fonts, or sequential document numbers across unrelated members. Compute each member's out-of-network foreign reimbursement total against the plan's trailing baseline for that member.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Domestic-presence conflict: on beneficiary x claimed foreign service date, compute the count of domestic claims or pharmacy fills on overlapping dates; fires when the count exceeds zero; action claim suspension. 2) Submitter cluster: on bank account, compute the distinct count of members, foreign facilities, and claim submissions received; fires when the count exceeds one member without a documented family relation; action payment suspension. 3) Unverifiable facility: on claim line, compute an exact match of the foreign provider name and address to a recognized international facility registry; fires on mismatch; action documentation request (ADR) before payment.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Hampshire
FraudEntity: LifeWorks Counseling Associates, PLLC; Dr. David Ferruolo (owner); Erik Alonso (excluded individual providing services)
SchemeSummary: LifeWorks, a New Hampshire telehealth mental health provider, and its owner Dr. David Ferruolo submitted Medicaid claims and received reimbursement for counseling services rendered by Erik Alonso, who had been excluded from federal health care programs by HHS-OIG, making the claims non-reimbursable; they agreed to pay $300,000 based on ability to pay, and Alonso separately pleaded guilty to one count of health care fraud on October 23, 2025.
WaysToIdentify: At credentialing, screen every rendering and supervised clinician NPI and SSN against the OIG LEIE and the state Medicaid exclusion list. At adjudication, match each claim's rendering NPI to the exclusion file effective date range for the date of service. Compare the entity's payroll and contractor roster on the CMS-855 disclosure against the clinicians actually named on claims. Recheck exclusion status monthly, since exclusions are added after initial enrolment. Count claims billed under a supervising NPI whose session notes name a different, non-enrolled counselor.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Exclusion match at adjudication: on claim line, compute an exact match of rendering, supervising, and ordering NPI or SSN to OIG LEIE and state exclusion files for the date of service; fires on any match; action prepay edit. 2) Roster refresh: on provider TIN x month, compute the count of disclosed employees or contractors newly appearing on LEIE since the last screening; fires when the count exceeds zero; action payment suspension. 3) Substitute-renderer gap: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute billed session counts minus sessions attributable to that NPI in the entity's scheduling records; fires when the difference is positive; action documentation request (ADR).

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Kentucky
FraudEntity: CompreCare Health LLC and its affiliates, d/b/a Meditelecare LLC (telehealth company)
State_County: Kentucky (Bowling Green/Louisville); Connecticut (company base); services provided in at least 17 states
SchemeSummary: Meditelecare billed Medicare for telehealth psychotherapy sessions that did not last the minimum time required for the billed time-based codes, and supported those claims with false time records; the allegations came from a qui tam whistleblower suit and were resolved for $358,514.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, sum the minimum minutes implied by time-based psychotherapy CPT codes per rendering NPI per day and compare with 24 hours. Compare each session's billed code to the telehealth platform connection log duration retained by the provider. Compute the share of sessions billed at the longer time-based code versus same-specialty peers in the same setting. Check for back-to-back session start times per rendering NPI that leave no gap for documentation. Count nursing facility beneficiaries receiving weekly psychotherapy without a supporting behavioral diagnosis in their other claims.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Daily minute impossibility: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute the sum of minimum minutes required by each billed time-based psychotherapy code; fires when the sum exceeds a physically possible workday or sessions overlap in minutes; action prepay edit. 2) Long-code concentration: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of longer-duration psychotherapy codes to all psychotherapy lines; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR) for platform connection logs. 3) Facility saturation: on facility x provider TIN x month, compute sessions per resident; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer facilities; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section; U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Florida
FraudEntity: Paul Wexler (operator of telemarketing company); Paul Bleignier (operator of telemarketing company; owner of clinical laboratory)
FraudTypeAll: kickback_Bribery For Referral; FakeEncounter; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud; IdentityFraud; Falsify certificate
SchemeSummary: Wexler and Bleignier ran a telemarketing company that solicited Medicare beneficiaries for medically unnecessary cancer genetic (CGx) testing and received kickbacks for referring those beneficiaries to laboratories, causing $17.3 million in Medicare billings and collecting $5.2 million in kickbacks. Separately, Bleignier enrolled his own clinical laboratory in Medicare while using other people's identities to conceal his 5%+ ownership, billing $3,012,156 in kickback-tainted, ineligible claims and being paid $916,106; the sentencing figures span both defendants (4 years for Wexler, 2 years for Bleignier, $1.2M forfeiture each, $5.2M restitution, plus $916,106 additional forfeiture for Bleignier).
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, check whether the ordering NPI on CGx claims has any prior evaluation-and-management encounter with the beneficiary in the payer's claim history. Count distinct beneficiary states per ordering NPI per week on genetic testing orders. Compare the beneficiary's cancer diagnosis and family history codes in other claims against the medical necessity criteria for hereditary cancer panels. At enrolment, verify all owners with 5 percent or greater interest on the CMS-855B against SSN, PECOS, and identity verification records. Compute the count of beneficiaries receiving the same CGx panel from more than one laboratory NPI within a year.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Order-encounter gap: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the last E/M claim between that orderer and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback window; action prepay edit. 2) Orderer dispersion: on ordering NPI x week, compute distinct beneficiary states and distinct laboratory NPIs on CGx orders; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action payment suspension. 3) Ownership identity verification: on billing TIN, compute an exact match of each disclosed 5 percent owner's name and SSN to identity and PECOS records including prior exclusions; fires on mismatch or undisclosed nominee; action claim suspension and site visit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
FraudEntity: Rashid Naqvi (owner/operator of Elite Diagnostics Inc. and Astro Diagnostics Inc.); Elite Diagnostics Inc.; Astro Diagnostics Inc.
State_County: Missouri - St. Louis (Eastern District of Missouri); Texas - Harris County (Houston area)
FraudTypeAll: Phantom Claims; IdentityFraud; kickback_Bribery For Referral; Wire Fraud; Falsify certificate; Device, DME
SchemeSummary: Naqvi's two labs submitted 22,898 claims to Medicare totaling $1,974,479 for COVID-19 test kits mailed to beneficiaries who never requested them, using Medicare numbers obtained through $488,435 in kickbacks to co-conspirators; some claims were for patients who had already died, and he produced false authorization records during Medicare audits to conceal the scheme.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, match each beneficiary on COVID test kit claims against the Death Master File for a date of death preceding the date of service. Check whether the ordering NPI has any prior encounter with the beneficiary in claim history before the mailed test kit. Count distinct beneficiaries per laboratory NPI per week whose residence ZIPs lie far outside the lab's enrolled service area. Compare the lab's weekly claim volume against its own trailing baseline since PECOS enrolment. Examine authorization records produced during audit for identical signatures or metadata across unrelated beneficiaries.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Deceased beneficiary edit: on claim line, compute days between date of service and the Death Master File date of death; fires when the service date follows death; action prepay edit. 2) Unsolicited mailing pattern: on laboratory NPI x week, compute the share of test kit claims with no prior E/M or order-linked encounter for the beneficiary; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer labs; action payment suspension. 3) Volume ramp: on billing NPI x week, compute claim counts divided by the provider's trailing 12-week baseline; fires when the ratio exceeds the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action claim suspension and site visit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Louisiana
FraudEntity: Murex Management, Inc. (MMI) (management company of ethanol marketing affiliate)
State_County: Texas - Collin County (Plano); Louisiana - Orleans Parish (New Orleans)
PayerName: First NBC Bank; a North Carolina bank
SchemeSummary: MMI and an ethanol producer ('Company A') allegedly created fictitious invoices purporting to reflect ethanol sales between the two companies ('buy/sells'), then sold those sham accounts receivable to financial institutions through a New Orleans online auction marketplace, generating cash flow for Company A and about $6.07 million in profit for MMI; approximately $1.2 billion in fake transactions ended in defaults causing about $73.07 million in losses to First NBC Bank and $8.33 million to a North Carolina bank.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, since the fraud is sale of fabricated commercial receivables to banks. The nearest detection route is receivables-auction underwriting comparing invoice counterparties, shipping and rail bills of lading, and tax filings for the purported ethanol deliveries. A second route is concentration analysis showing nearly all receivables flowing between two affiliated counterparties with circular payment timing.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) Counterparty circularity: on obligor pair, compute the share of auctioned receivables between the same two entities and the count lacking independent delivery documentation; fires when concentration exceeds the platform's calibrated percentile; action funding suspension pending documentation.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division Fraud Section; U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas
FraudEntity: Jorge Zamora-Quezada, M.D. (rheumatologist)
State_County: Texas - Hidalgo County (Mission); Rio Grande Valley
PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid; TRICARE; Blue Cross Blue Shield
FraudTypeAll: FakeEncounter; Falsify certificate; Drug_Prescriptions; Phantom Claims
SchemeSummary: Rheumatologist falsely diagnosed patients with rheumatoid arthritis so he could bill Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE and Blue Cross Blue Shield for medically unnecessary injections, infusions, x-rays, MRIs and other procedures, fabricating medical records (including using ultrasound images of employees as patient documentation) to support the diagnoses and defeat insurer audits and a grand jury subpoena; over $118 million billed and $28 million paid.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compute the share of a rheumatologist's panel carrying a rheumatoid arthritis diagnosis relative to same-specialty peers in the same state. Count infusion and injection J-code units per attributed beneficiary per year against peer distributions. Check whether serologic testing such as rheumatoid factor or anti-CCP appears in the beneficiary's claim history before biologic infusion claims begin. Compare imaging volume, including MRI and diagnostic ultrasound, per beneficiary against peer rheumatologists. Detect identical ultrasound image files or duplicate report text across different beneficiaries during documentation review.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Diagnosis prevalence outlier: on rendering NPI x year, compute the share of attributed beneficiaries with a rheumatoid arthritis diagnosis code; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action documentation request (ADR). 2) Infusion without confirmatory testing: on beneficiary x provider NPI, compute the count of biologic infusion lines preceded by zero rheumatoid serology claims in the lookback; fires when the count exceeds zero; action prior-authorisation requirement. 3) Duplicate-documentation detection: on provider NPI, compute the distinct-hash count of submitted imaging files divided by the count of imaging claims; fires when the ratio falls below one; action payment suspension and postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Texas
FraudEntity: Jeffrey Paul Madison (hospital CEO, Little River Healthcare); Susan L. Hertzberg (Boston Heart Diagnostics executive); Matthew John Theiler (laboratory sales executive); David Weldon Kraus (laboratory sales executive); Thomas Gray Hardaway; Jeffrey Paul Parnell; Laura Spain Howard; Todd Dean Cook; William Todd Hickman; Christopher Roland Gonzales; Ruben Daniel Marioni; Jordan Joseph Perkins; Elizabeth Ruth Seymour; Linh Ba Nguyen; Thuy Ngoc Nguyen; Joseph Gil Bolin; Heriberto Salinas; Hong Davis; Robert O'Neal (marketer); Peter J. Bennett (attorney, money launderer); Little River Healthcare; Stamford Memorial Hospital; Boston Heart Diagnostics
State_County: Texas - Milam County (Rockdale); Texas - Jones County (Stamford); Massachusetts - Middlesex County (Framingham)
PayerName: Medicare; Medicaid; other federal health care programs
FraudTypeAll: kickback_Bribery For Referral; Wire Fraud; Upcoding
SchemeSummary: Two rural Texas hospitals (Little River Healthcare and Stamford Memorial) partnered with clinical lab Boston Heart Diagnostics: BHD processed cardiovascular lipid blood tests for a fee while the hospitals billed insurers for them as higher-paying hospital outpatient services. The hospitals paid a share of lab revenue to marketers running sham management services organizations, which passed kickbacks to referring physicians disguised as MSO 'investment returns'; one attorney laundered at least $2,724,080 of kickback proceeds through sham trusts, shell corporations and his law firm's IOLTA account. Figures span multiple defendants: Madison received 36 months and agreed to pay $5,343,630 under the FCA; Theiler 18 months and a $75,000 fine; Kraus 22 months and a $25,000 fine.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compare the beneficiary residence ZIP and referring physician address against the rural hospital's service area for outpatient lipid panel claims. Compute the share of a critical access hospital's outpatient lab revenue derived from specimens not collected on its own campus. Check whether the reference laboratory performing the test is the entity of record versus the hospital billing under outpatient rates. Cross-reference referring physician NPIs against ownership or investment interests in management services organizations disclosed on enrolment and Open Payments. Compute the ratio of lab lines to face-to-face encounters for each referring NPI at that hospital.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Pass-through lab detection: on hospital NPI x month, compute the share of outpatient lab claims where the beneficiary has no same-facility encounter within the surrounding days; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer hospitals; action prepay edit. 2) Non-local referral geography: on referring NPI x hospital NPI, compute the mean distance between referring practice address in NPPES and the hospital's enrolled location; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer referral patterns; action claim suspension. 3) Investment-linked referral: on referring NPI, compute the count of lab lines billed to hospitals sharing an MSO payment relationship in disclosure or Open Payments records; fires when the count exceeds zero; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Tennessee
FraudEntity: Shelby Lynn Hill (health insurance broker)
FraudTypeAll: Covid or General Loan Fraud; Wire Fraud; IdentityFraud
SchemeSummary: Hill, a health insurance broker, obtained a $220,645 PPP loan for a fictitious cattle farm (Plateau Angus Farms) by submitting fake W-2s and Tennessee Secretary of State records claiming 14 employees and $88,000 monthly payroll - listing prospective health insurance customers' identities as employees without authorization - plus a $42,700 PPP loan for a second fictitious company, and misused PPP proceeds of a third entity (Shelby Lynn Hill, MD PLLC) to install a personal swimming pool.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, since this is pandemic loan fraud using fabricated payroll for nonexistent businesses. The nearest detection route is lender comparison of applicant payroll schedules against IRS Form 941 filings and state unemployment insurance wage records before disbursement. A second route is cross-application matching of listed employee SSNs appearing simultaneously on unrelated applicants and on the broker's insurance client rosters.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) Payroll verification mismatch: on loan application EIN, compute the difference between claimed monthly payroll and IRS 941 plus state wage-record payroll for the same quarters; fires on any material mismatch or absent filings; action disbursement hold pending verification.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Louisiana; U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section
FraudEntity: Darrion Denard Brooks
State_County: Louisiana - East Baton Rouge Parish (Baton Rouge); Texas; Florida; Georgia; Tennessee
SchemeSummary: Brooks and co-conspirators allegedly used fictitious patient identification information and the DEA registration numbers and identifying data of at least five medical professionals, without authorization, to present at least 11 fraudulent prescriptions for codeine and other controlled substances at eight pharmacies in five states, then resold the drugs on the street.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, match the prescriber DEA number on controlled-substance claims to the registrant's registered state and practice address in the DEA file. Check whether the presenting beneficiary identifier exists in the payer's eligibility file and matches name and date of birth. Count distinct pharmacies in distinct states filling schedule prescriptions under one prescriber DEA number within days via the PDMP. Compare the prescribed codeine NDC and quantity against that prescriber's own trailing prescribing baseline. Detect sequential or duplicated prescription serial numbers presented at multiple pharmacies in the same chain's dispensing records.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Prescriber geographic dispersion: on prescriber DEA number x week, compute the count of distinct dispensing pharmacy states in PDMP and claims data; fires when the count exceeds the prescriber's trailing baseline or peer percentile; action prepay edit and prescriber verification call. 2) Eligibility identity mismatch: on claim line, compute an exact match of member ID, name, and date of birth to the eligibility file; fires on any mismatch for a controlled-substance NDC; action claim suspension. 3) Prescriber baseline break: on prescriber DEA x NDC schedule, compute weekly dispensed quantity divided by the trailing 12-week baseline; fires when the ratio exceeds the calibrated percentile; action payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section; U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of Texas
FraudEntity: Dehshid "David" Nourian (pharmacist, owner/operator of three compounding pharmacies)
State_County: Texas - Tarrant County (Fort Worth); Texas - Tarrant County (Arlington)
PayerName: U.S. Department of Labor Office of Workers' Compensation Programs; Blue Cross Blue Shield
FraudTypeAll: Drug_Prescriptions; kickback_Bribery For Referral; FakeEncounter; Wire Fraud; Tax, Payroll or Coupon Fraud
SchemeSummary: Nourian and co-conspirators paid doctors millions in bribes and kickbacks to prescribe medically unnecessary compound pain creams to injured federal workers; the creams were mixed by untrained teenagers in pharmacy back rooms at ~$15 per prescription and billed to DOL-OWCP and Blue Cross Blue Shield for as much as $16,000 per prescription, totaling over $145 million billed and $90 million paid, with proceeds laundered through shell/holding companies and $24 million in taxes evaded. Restitution of over $115 million plus $405 million forfeiture were imposed.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compute the paid amount per compounded cream prescription against ingredient acquisition cost benchmarks and peer pharmacy distributions. Count the share of a pharmacy's workers' compensation claims originating from a small set of prescriber NPIs. Compare prescriber payments recorded in the pharmacy's disclosed contracts, Open Payments, and shell-company remittances against referral volume. Check whether each injured worker had a documented failure of standard oral analgesics in the claim history before compound approval. Detect refills authorized without any intervening prescriber encounter in the workers' compensation claim record.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Cost-to-charge outlier: on claim line, compute billed amount divided by benchmark ingredient cost for the compound NDC set; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer compounding pharmacies; action prior-authorisation requirement. 2) Prescriber concentration and payment link: on pharmacy NPI x prescriber NPI, compute referred claim dollars alongside dollars paid to that prescriber or affiliated entity from the pharmacy's bank accounts; fires when both exceed the calibrated percentile versus peers; action payment suspension. 3) Step-therapy gap: on beneficiary x compound claim, compute the count of prior paid oral analgesic fills in the lookback; fires when the count is zero; action prepay edit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Oklahoma
FraudEntity: Nnamdi Felix Udeagha
State_County: Oklahoma - Eastern District of Oklahoma (Chickasaw Nation); Texas - Humble
SchemeSummary: Business email compromise scheme: conspirators sent the Chickasaw Nation Department of Health emails posing as a legitimate vendor directing payment to bank accounts opened by the conspirators; Udeagha supplied the receiving bank account information used to collect and distribute the diverted payments.
WaysToIdentify: There is no health care claim and no adjudication point, since funds were diverted by impersonating a vendor in email rather than by billing. The nearest detection route is accounts-payable verification of any bank-account change request through a callback to the vendor contact of record, not the requesting email. A second route is matching the new beneficiary bank account and routing number against the vendor master file and against accounts newly opened in unrelated names.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) Vendor bank-change verification: on vendor master record, compute the count of payment-instruction changes with no out-of-band callback confirmation and the days since the account was opened; fires when a change is unverified or the account is newly opened; action payment hold pending verification.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Kentucky; U.S. District Court for the Western District of Kentucky
FraudEntity: The Arthritis Knee Pain Centers (AKPC); Dr. John Rush (owner and Chief Executive Officer)
SchemeSummary: Civil False Claims Act complaint alleging that a knee-injection clinic and its owner-physician doubled billable visits by treating each knee of bilateral osteoarthritis patients on separate dates rather than the same visit, and billed Medicare for millions of milliliters of single-use contrast dye claimed as discarded when it was actually reused on other patients.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, bilateral knee patients show right and left injection CPT 20610/20611 lines on separate dates instead of one date with modifier 50. The rendering NPI's ratio of split-date bilateral injections to same-date RT/LT pairs far exceeds same-specialty peers in remittance history. JW-modifier discarded milliliters on the contrast NDC exceed what one single-use vial per patient can yield. Billed drug volume per quarter exceeds vials acquired per wholesaler pedigree and purchase invoices. Repeat E/M and facility visit counts per beneficiary per year sit above orthopedic peer norms.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Bilateral split-visit ratio: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the share of beneficiaries with right-knee and left-knee injection CPT lines on different dates within 30 days divided by same-date RT/LT pairs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action prepay edit on the second date of service. 2) Discard-to-vial reconciliation: on rendering NPI x HCPCS x month, compute total JW discarded units divided by administered units against labeled single-use vial size for the NDC; fires when discard exceeds one vial per patient physically allows; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Purchase-versus-billed volume: on TIN x NDC x quarter, compute billed milliliters minus milliliters evidenced in wholesaler acquisition records; fires when billed exceeds acquired; action payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Pennsylvania
FraudEntity: Scottie Girl, LLC d/b/a The Breastfeeding Shop (DME supplier); Patricia Gatter (owner)
SchemeSummary: The United States alleged that The Breastfeeding Shop, a DME supplier, billed TRICARE hundreds of dollars more per breast pump than it charged Pennsylvania Medicaid (a prohibited dual fee schedule), and unbundled accessories already included in the standard pre-packaged breast pump kit by billing TRICARE separately for each item as a replacement part; the company and its owner collectively pay $1 million.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compare the supplier's submitted charge for HCPCS E0603 breast pumps against its charges to state Medicaid for the same code. Check whether accessory HCPCS lines (A4281-A4286) are billed on the same date as the pump kit already containing them. Look for accessory lines coded as replacement parts with no prior pump dispense date in the beneficiary's claim history. Compare the supplier's charge-to-allowed spread against same-code peers in the DMEPOS remittance file. Verify the product model billed against the manufacturer kit contents listed on the CMS-855S product line at enrolment.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Dual fee schedule differential: on supplier NPI x HCPCS, compute the submitted charge to this payer minus the same supplier's submitted charge to other payers for the identical code and date window; fires when the differential exceeds zero after allowed rounding; action prepay edit. 2) Kit component unbundling: on claim line, compute the count of accessory HCPCS codes billed on the same date of service as the pump base code that are listed as included kit contents; fires when that count is above zero; action prepay edit. 3) Phantom replacement: on beneficiary x supplier NPI, compute days between the accessory 'replacement' line and the earliest paid pump dispense; fires when no prior pump dispense exists; action claim suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of New Hampshire (with Districts of Vermont and Maine; New England Strike Force)

WaysToIdentify: At enrolment and monthly, match every CMS-855 owner, officer and managing-employee SSN against OIG LEIE and state exclusion lists. At adjudication, check brace HCPCS claims for beneficiaries whose ordering NPI has no prior encounter claim. Compare the ordering physician NPI's own claim submissions and NPPES contact data against the volume of orders attributed to that NPI. Screen pharmacy claims for NDCs whose lot pedigree does not appear in ARCOS or licensed wholesaler purchase records.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Exclusion match on ownership: on TIN x disclosed individual, compute exact match of name, date of birth and SSN against OIG LEIE and state exclusion files at enrolment and each revalidation; fires on any exact registry match; action payment suspension and enrolment revocation. 2) Straw-owner divergence: on supplier NPI, compute the count of distinct individuals appearing as payment-account signatories or wire beneficiaries who are absent from the CMS-855 ownership section; fires when that count is above zero; action site visit. 3) Order without encounter: on claim line x ordering NPI, compute days since the most recent E/M or telehealth encounter claim between that NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists in the lookback; action prepay edit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of North Carolina; U.S. District Court for the Western District of North Carolina
FraudEntity: Benson I. Ejindu (operator of durable medical equipment business)
SchemeSummary: Complaint alleges Ejindu, through a DME business operated under different names, billed North Carolina Medicaid for high-reimbursing specialized nutritional formula for rare inherited metabolic disorders while recipients actually received lower-reimbursing retail drinks such as Ensure, PediaSure, Boost and Glucerna.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compare the high-reimbursement metabolic formula HCPCS (B4157 enteral, inborn-error formula codes) against the beneficiary's diagnosis history for an inherited metabolic disorder ICD-10 code. Check whether any claim from a metabolic specialist or geneticist NPI appears in the beneficiary's other claims. Reconcile units of specialty formula billed against the supplier's wholesaler purchase invoices for those NDCs. Look for a single TIN operating under several DBA names and NPIs at the same service address in PECOS. Compare the supplier's share of inborn-error formula codes to statewide DME peers in remittance history.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Formula-diagnosis mismatch: on claim line, compute whether a qualifying inherited metabolic disorder ICD-10 code appears on the beneficiary's paid claims in the prior 12 months; fires when no such diagnosis exists for a specialty metabolic formula HCPCS; action prepay edit. 2) Product acquisition reconciliation: on supplier NPI x HCPCS x quarter, compute billed units minus units evidenced by wholesaler or manufacturer purchase records for that formula NDC; fires when billed exceeds purchased; action payment suspension. 3) Specialty formula concentration: on supplier NPI x quarter, compute the ratio of inborn-error formula units to total enteral nutrition units; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty peers; action postpay audit.

SchemeSummary: The United States, intervening in a qui tam suit, alleges that Aetna, Elevance/Anthem and Humana paid hundreds of millions of dollars in kickbacks to broker organizations eHealth, GoHealth and SelectQuote in exchange for steering Medicare beneficiaries into their Medicare Advantage plans regardless of suitability, and that Aetna and Humana threatened to withhold those payments to pressure brokers to enroll fewer disabled beneficiaries perceived as less profitable.

Enrollment files can be tested for the disabled-under-65 share of each broker's enrollments versus that broker's overall book.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) Broker compensation cap test: on plan contract ID x broker TIN x plan year, compute total payments reported in administrative cost and marketing filings divided by enrollments attributed to that broker, compared to the published CMS compensation limit; fires when per-enrollee payment exceeds the limit; action postpay audit and referral. 2) Disability steering skew: on broker TIN x plan contract ID x quarter, compute the share of new enrollees with an original-reason-for-entitlement disability indicator relative to the county eligible population share; fires when below the calibrated percentile versus peer brokers in the same counties; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Louisiana
FraudEntity: John Christopher Barrilleaux (social worker)
SchemeSummary: A Thibodaux social worker submitted false claims to private insurers for millions of dollars of counseling/healthcare services never provided, and created fake patient notes to support the bills; ordered to pay $4,592,650 restitution plus a $100 special assessment and sentenced to 30 months.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, compute daily billed psychotherapy minutes per rendering NPI from CPT 90837, 90834 and 90853 units against a 24-hour day. Compare the rendering NPI's counseling dates of service against beneficiary claims showing inpatient stays or out-of-area services the same day. Check for identical session-note text and identical start times across many beneficiaries in ADR-returned documentation. Look for beneficiaries with no other behavioral health claims from any provider surrounding the billed episode. Compare the solo licensee's annual paid encounter count against state licence board scope and same-specialty peer volume.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Impossible clinician day: on rendering NPI x date of service, compute total service minutes implied by billed psychotherapy CPT time units; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours or the provider's own trailing baseline by the calibrated margin; action prepay edit. 2) Patient corroboration gap: on beneficiary x rendering NPI, compute the count of other providers' claims within 90 days of the billed counseling episode; fires when zero corroborating claims exist and session count is above the peer percentile; action documentation request (ADR). 3) Note duplication: on rendering NPI, compute the distinct-value count of session-note text hashes divided by the number of billed sessions in ADR responses; fires when the ratio falls below the calibrated threshold; action payment suspension.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Middle District of Louisiana
FraudEntity: Kevan Andre Hills; Devin Tyrone Stampley, Jr.; Asia Deshan Guess
State_County: Louisiana - East Baton Rouge Parish (Baton Rouge)
PayerName: Medicaid; Paycheck Protection Program; Economic Injury Disaster Loan Program; CARES Act unemployment (Louisiana Workforce Commission; Maine Department of Labor)
FraudTypeAll: Drug_Prescriptions; IdentityFraud; Covid or General Loan Fraud; Falsify certificate; Wire Fraud
SchemeSummary: Three defendants submitted fraudulent prescriptions for controlled substances (Promethazine with Codeine, Hydrocodone) to pharmacies using the stolen DEA registration numbers and identifying information of licensed physicians, causing Medicaid to be billed for filling them, with the drugs resold; Stampley also burglarized a Louisiana pharmacy. The same defendants separately sought at least $293,498 in PPP/EIDL/CARES unemployment funds using falsified bank statements and tax forms (receiving at least $87,663), while Guess sought $125,978 in PUA benefits from Louisiana and Maine workforce agencies using falsified employment and residency details (receiving at least $15,859). Amounts span multiple defendants.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, match the prescriber DEA number on the pharmacy claim against the DEA registration file for schedule authority, address and expiry. Compare the prescriber's practice ZIP in NPPES to the dispensing pharmacy ZIP and the member's residence ZIP. Count distinct beneficiaries receiving promethazine-with-codeine or hydrocodone NDCs from one prescriber DEA in a rolling week. Check whether the prescriber has any prior claim relationship with the beneficiary in the payer's claim history. Compare pharmacy dispensed controlled-substance volume against ARCOS and wholesaler purchase records for the same NDCs.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) DEA registry validation: on claim line, compute exact match of prescriber DEA number, schedule authority and registration status against the DEA file on the fill date; fires on any mismatch or expired registration; action prepay edit. 2) Prescriber-pharmacy distance and burst: on prescriber DEA x week, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries and distinct pharmacies for controlled-substance NDCs plus median miles between prescriber and pharmacy ZIPs; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-specialty prescribers; action claim suspension. 3) No prior relationship: on beneficiary x prescriber NPI, compute days since the last paid encounter claim between them; fires when no encounter exists before a schedule II or III fill; action prior-authorisation requirement.

SchemeSummary: The three defendants submitted fraudulent prescriptions for controlled substances (Promethazine with Codeine, Hydrocodone) to pharmacies using the stolen DEA registration numbers and identifying information of licensed physicians and other providers, causing Medicaid to be billed for filling them, and Stampley also burglarized a Louisiana pharmacy to obtain drugs for resale.
