JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, Fraud Section
FraudEntity: Dr. José Alzadon (medical director, Kentucky Addiction Centers); Michael Bregenzer (CEO); Barbie Vanhoose (billing manager); Kentucky Addiction Centers (KAC)
State_County: Kentucky - Winchester (Clark County); Paducah (McCracken County); Paintsville (Johnson County); London (Laurel County)
FraudTypeAll: Phantom Claims; Upcoding; IdentityFraud; Drug_Prescriptions; Benefit & Eligibility Fraud
SchemeSummary: Operators of Kentucky Addiction Centers opioid treatment clinics billed Medicare and Kentucky Medicaid over $8 million for services never performed or billed at higher complexity than delivered, and billed services and Suboxone prescriptions under the identity and DEA registration of Alzadon's elderly father to bypass Alzadon's credentialing problems, even though the father never saw the patients. WaysToIdentify: At credentialing, compare the rendering NPI's date of birth and NPPES record against active practice indicators such as recent continuing-education or other payer claims. Check whether the credentialed rendering NPI ever appears on facility sign-in, EVV or timesheet records returned under ADR. Compare the clinic's mix of high-complexity E/M and OTP bundle codes against opioid treatment program peers. Screen owners and managing employees on the CMS-855 against state board discipline files and OIG LEIE.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Ghost prescriber load: on prescriber NPI x date of service, compute the count of distinct beneficiaries with billed encounters or buprenorphine prescriptions divided by available clinical hours; fires when implied minutes per patient fall below a physically possible visit length; action prepay edit. 2) Credential substitution: on clinic TIN x rendering NPI x month, compute the ratio of claims billed under the highest-volume rendering NPI to that NPI's documented on-site hours in timesheets; fires when billed encounters exceed documented hours; action documentation request (ADR) then payment suspension. 3) Complexity drift: on rendering NPI x quarter, compute the share of level-4 and level-5 E/M plus high-intensity counseling codes; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus opioid treatment program peers; action postpay audit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Michigan

SchemeSummary: Three defendants submitted fraudulent Paycheck Protection Program loan applications for several business entities, misrepresenting payroll data, falsely certifying permissible use of funds, and supporting the applications with fictitious payroll, health insurance, bank and tax records; they obtained over $3 million, of which over $2.1 million has been seized/recovered.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Massachusetts
FraudEntity: Amy Winslow (former CEO, Magellan Diagnostics, Inc.); Hossein Maleknia (former COO); Reba Daoust (former Director of Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs); Magellan Diagnostics, Inc. (medical device company)
FraudTypeAll: Other - FDA Submission Fraud; Device, DME
SchemeSummary: Three Magellan Diagnostics executives concealed and misled customers and the FDA about a malfunction in the company's LeadCare II and LeadCare Ultra blood lead testing devices that produced inaccurately low results for venous blood samples, keeping the misbranded devices in interstate commerce to protect sales; thousands of children and other patients received inaccurate lead test results before the FDA forced a recall. All three pleaded guilty (two to introducing misbranded devices, one to false statements); sentencing was pending.
WaysToIdentify: There is no payer claim mechanic here, since the harm is device misbranding rather than billing, so adjudication offers no hook. The nearest route is the FDA Medical Device Reporting database showing complaint clusters for one device model against the manufacturer's own submitted correction reports. Laboratory proficiency-testing results filed under CLIA can be compared across analyzers for systematic low bias on venous specimens.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) Device complaint divergence: on device model x quarter, compute the count of MDR complaints and CLIA proficiency-testing failures citing low venous results divided by installed base, versus the manufacturer's reported corrections; fires when complaint rate exceeds the calibrated percentile versus comparable assay platforms; action site visit by the regulator. 2) Confirmatory retest discordance: on laboratory CLIA number x quarter, compute the share of venous blood lead results later contradicted by a reference-method retest; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus peer laboratories; action postpay audit of the testing program.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of New York
FraudEntity: Ciera Washington; Raven White; Bryan Otero
State_County: New York - Northern District of New York (including Albany); New York - Bronx County; New Jersey - Wood-Ridge (Bergen County)
SchemeSummary: Indictment alleges White and Otero supplied Washington with stolen names, dates of birth and Medicaid ID numbers, which Washington used to submit fraudulent prescriptions to pharmacies across the Northeast; rideshare drivers were dispatched to collect the Medicaid-funded medications, which were then delivered to Otero and other buyers who paid Washington. HHS-OIG states false claims were submitted for both transportation and medications.
WaysToIdentify: At adjudication, count distinct pharmacy NPIs filling for the same Medicaid ID across states within a short window. Compare the member's residence ZIP on the eligibility file with the dispensing pharmacy ZIP and the prescriber's NPPES address. Check whether the prescriber NPI on the fill has any prior encounter claim with that member. Match delivery or courier transportation claims to a pharmacy pickup rather than an authorized medical appointment in the trip record. Look for repeated same-day fills of high-value NDCs for members with no supporting diagnosis in claim history.
FeaturesToCreate: 1) Cross-state pharmacy dispersion: on beneficiary Medicaid ID x rolling 30 days, compute the count of distinct pharmacy NPIs and distinct states with paid fills; fires when above the calibrated percentile versus same-plan members; action claim suspension. 2) Prescriber relationship gap: on claim line, compute days since the last paid encounter between the prescriber NPI and the beneficiary; fires when no encounter exists before a high-cost NDC fill; action prepay edit. 3) Trip-destination mismatch: on transportation claim line, compute whether the trip destination address matches an enrolled medical facility in PECOS rather than a pharmacy or residence; fires on exact registry mismatch; action prepay edit.

JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Western District of Pennsylvania
FraudEntity: Drew Pierce (former CEO of Primary Health Network); Jack Laeng (former CEO of Primary Health Network); Mark Marriott (former facilities manager); TopCoat (company owned by the defendants)
State_County: Pennsylvania - Mercer County (Sharon); Pennsylvania - Mercer County (West Middlesex); Pennsylvania - Mercer County (Sharpsville)

SchemeSummary: Two former CEOs and a facilities manager of Primary Health Network, a non-profit community medical provider in Sharon, PA, inserted their own company TopCoat between PHN and its vendors, paying the vendor and billing PHN a marked-up amount (on one 2017 deal, over $200,000 more than the true vendor cost), and issued invoices for work TopCoat never performed, splitting the spread via checks from TopCoat's account. In a separate scheme, Pierce, Laeng and a co-conspirator caused PHN to contract with a third party that kicked back 50% of its fees—more than $1.7 million between 2013 and 2020—to an entity they controlled. Amounts and pleas span three defendants; sentencings are set for March 2026.
WaysToIdentify: There is no patient claim and no adjudication point, because the loss ran through vendor invoicing at a grant-funded clinic. The nearest route is matching vendor payee TINs on the entity's accounts-payable ledger against officers and family members disclosed on IRS Form 990 Schedule L related-party filings. Grant cost reports can be tested by comparing invoiced vendor prices against the underlying subcontractor invoices for the same work order.
FeaturesToCreate: No payer-side control applies. 1) Related-party payee match: on payee TIN x fiscal year, compute exact match of the payee's registered officers against the organization's officers and Form 990 disclosures; fires on any exact registry match not disclosed as a related-party transaction; action postpay audit of cost reports. 2) Markup spread: on vendor invoice, compute invoiced amount minus the underlying subcontractor invoice for the same work order divided by that cost; fires when the markup exceeds the calibrated percentile versus comparable service contracts; action documentation request. 3) Percentage kickback pattern: on contracted third party x year, compute the share of received fees transferred out to a single affiliated entity; fires when that share approaches a fixed split of total fees; action postpay audit.

SchemeSummary: Owners and staff of a Medicaid-enrolled home health agency billed Virginia Medicaid for private duty nursing, personal care and respite services that were never provided or were billed in excess of what was provided; parents/guardians of patients were paid cash for pre-signed blank nursing notes that employees (including the director of nursing) filled out to document the fictitious visits. Check that the nurse listed on the visit note holds an active licence on the state board file for that date. FeaturesToCreate: 1) EVV-to-claim reconciliation: on beneficiary x date of service x agency NPI, compute billed units minus units supported by matched EVV check-in and check-out records; fires when billed units exceed verified units; action prepay edit. 2) Caregiver hour impossibility: on caregiver identifier x week, compute total billed service hours across all beneficiaries; fires when the total exceeds 24 hours in any day or the hours reported on payroll timesheets; action claim suspension. 3) Authorization overage: on beneficiary x service HCPCS x authorization period, compute cumulative paid units divided by prior-authorised units; fires when the ratio exceeds one; action prepay edit.

FraudEntity: Jeremie Vargas Ramirez (de facto owner of NOVA DME); Jordana Lee Arpa (nominal President and CEO); Dennis William Karnes (health care consultant/lead broker); Kynetic Medical Group d/b/a NOVA DME (DME supplier)
